explanation: Abhayanand Mishra v. State of Bihar (AIR 1961 SC 1698) is a landmark case defining the boundaries between preparation and attempt under Section 511 IPC (Section 62 BNS). Option (A) maintained strictly per source text key.

subject: BNS
question: The offence of rape is defined in which Section of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 ?
explanation: Section 63 of BNS defines rape (replacing Old IPC Section 375).

subject: BNS
question: Under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, sexual intercourse by a man with a woman who is not his wife with her consent is a rape, if she is below the age of :-
explanation: Section 63 of BNS sets the age of consent for a woman at 18 years.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' commits sexual intercourse with his own wife aged under 15 year with her consent, it is :-
explanation: Under Section 63 of BNS (and reaffirmed by the Supreme Court in Independent Thought v. UOI), sexual intercourse with a wife under 18 years constitutes rape regardless of consent.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' promises to marry 'B' his student and inducted her to cohabit with him. He has given her a false assurance of marriage and also fraudulently gone through certain ceremonies of marriage, making 'B' believe that she was a lawfully wedded wife of 'A'. Later 'A' refused to recognize her as his wife. What offence has been committed by 'A'?
explanation: Consent obtained by deceitful means or false promise of marriage vitiates consent under Section 63 BNS (read with Section 69 BNS).

subject: BNS
question: 'A' has sexual intercourse with a widow with her consent. 'A' is guilty of :-
explanation: Under Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS), consensual sexual intercourse between adults does not constitute an offence unless accompanied by vitiating factors such as fraud or coercion.

subject: BNS
question: "Illicit intercourse" implies :-
options: Sex between two persons not united by lawful marriage
explanation: Legally, 'illicit intercourse' denotes sexual intercourse occurring between two individuals who are not lawfully married to each other.

subject: BNS
question: What is not an offence under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Except where the wife is under 18 years of age, marital rape between an adult husband and wife remains protected by Exception 2 to Section 63 of BNS and is not classified as an offence under the code.

subject: BNS
question: In which of the following case Exception 2 of Section 375 of Indian Penal Code [Now, Exception 2 of Section 63 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023] was under challenge (when age of wife was 15 years) :-
options: Tuka Ram & Anr. vs. State of Maharashtra
Mukesh & Anr. vs. State of N.C.T. of Delhi
Independent Thought vs. Union of India, WP (Civil) No. 382/13
Harpal Singh vs. State of Haryana
explanation: In Independent Thought v. Union of India, the writ petition challenged the statutory exception that permitted sexual intercourse with a minor wife between 15 and 18 years of age.

subject: BNS
question: In which of the following judgment the Supreme Court has held that exception two, to Section 375 IPC (Now, Exception 2 of Section 63 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023) is violative of the rights of the girl child below 18 years ?
options: Independent thought Vs. Union of India.
S.R. Sukumar Vs. S. Sunaad Raghuram
Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar
Rameshchandra Ambalal Joshi Vs. State of Gujrat.
explanation: The Supreme Court in Independent Thought v. Union of India (2017) struck down the exception shielding husbands from rape charges where the minor wife was aged between 15 and 18 years.

subject: BNS
question: Supreme Court has interpreted the Exception 2 to S. 375 of IPC [Now, Exception 2 of Section 63 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023] as "Sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his own wife, the wife not below 18 years, is not rape". The case is:-
options: Independent Thought Vs. Union of India
Youth Advocate Association Vs. Union of India
Lilly Thomas Vs. Union of India
Alakh Alok Shrivastava Vs. Union of India
explanation: The Supreme Court read down the exception in Independent Thought v. Union of India, raising the marital consent threshold for wives to 18 years.

subject: BNS
question: In which case Supreme Court has propounded that intercourse committed by husband with his wife below the age of 18 years, is rape :-
options: Suresh Kumar Kaushal Vs. Naz foundation (India) Trust, (2014) 1 SCC 1
Independent thought Vs. Union of India, (2017) 10 SCC 800
P.U.C.L. Vs. Union of India, (2010) 14 SCC 245
Shreya Singhal Vs. Union of India, AIR 2015 SC 1523
explanation: The landmark ruling of Independent Thought v. Union of India (2017) established that sexual acts by a man with his wife under 18 years of age constitute rape.

subject: BNS
question: In which of the following cases did the Supreme Court issue guidelines to render assistance to rape victims?
options: Vijayan v. State of Kerala (2008) 14 SCC 763
Delhi Domestic Working Women's Forum v. Union of India 1995 SCC (1) 14
Zakir v. Sate of M.P. (2009) 6 SCC 646
State of Madhya Pradesh v. Rameshwar (2005) 2 SCC 373
explanation: In Delhi Domestic Working Women's Forum v. Union of India (1995), the Supreme Court laid down detailed directives regarding legal representation, compensation, and support systems for victims of rape.

subject: BNS
question: In which of the following recent case, the Supreme Court prohibited "Two-Finger Test" in rape cases and warned that persons conducting such tests will be held guilty of misconduct :-
options: Sumitha Pradeep Vs. Arun Kumar C.K & Anr., AIR 2022 SC 5705
Subramanya Vs. State of Karnataka, AIR 2022 SC 5110
Ketan Kantilal Seth Vs. State of Gujarat & Ors., AIR 2022 SC 4187
State of Jharkhand Vs. Shailendra Kumar Rai @ Pandav Rai, AIR 2022 SC 5393
explanation: In State of Jharkhand v. Shailendra Kumar Rai (2022), the Supreme Court strictly banned the regressive 'two-finger test' and declared it a violation of a victim's dignity and privacy.

subject: BNS
question: In which Section of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 punishment for offence of rape is provided ?
explanation: Section 64 of BNS prescribes the penal consequences for committing rape, replacing Old IPC Section 376.

subject: BNS
question: In which of the following cases, there may be presumption to absence of consent in prosecution for rape :-
explanation: Aggravated forms of rape listed under Section 64(2) BNS trigger statutory presumptions regarding the absence of consent under evidence laws.

subject: BNS
question: Which section of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 will be attracted if a public servant, commits rape on a woman in his custody ?
explanation: Section 64(2)(b) of BNS specifically covers custodial rape committed by a public servant taking advantage of official position.

subject: BNS
question: The minimum punishment for the offence of rape under Section 64 Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is :-
explanation: Section 64(1) of BNS mandates a minimum punishment of rigorous imprisonment for ten years, which may extend to life imprisonment.

subject: BNS
question: What is the maximum punishment provided for the offence under Section 64 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
options: imprisonment for the remainder of accused's natural life
explanation: Under Section 64, the maximum punishment for standard rape extends to imprisonment for life, defined as the remainder of that person's natural life.

subject: BNS
question: Any fine imposed under Section 65(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 shall be
options: deposited in the government treasury and shall be used for the medical expenses and rehabilitation of the victim
paid to the parents or guardian of the victim
expended for the treatment and legal expenses of the victim
explanation: The statutory scheme under BNS specifies that fines levied under Section 65 are to be paid directly to the victim to meet medical and rehabilitation needs.

subject: BNS
question: Section 65(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 provides for :-
options: punishment for rape on woman under twelve years of age
punishment for gang rape on woman under sixteen years of age
punishment for gang rape on woman under twelve years of age
punishment for causing death or resulting in persistent vegetative state of victim
explanation: Section 65(2) of BNS deals with punishment for committing rape on a girl child under twelve years of age.

subject: BNS
question: What is the maximum punishment for rape on woman under twelve years of age under Section 65(2) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Section 65(2) prescribes rigorous imprisonment for a minimum of 20 years, extending to life imprisonment or death penalty.

subject: BNS
question: Which of the following Sections of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 punishes for causing death or resulting in persistent vegetative state of victim during the commission of offence of Rape?
explanation: Section 66 of BNS (Old IPC Section 376A) penalizes causing the death of a victim or inflicting injuries that reduce the victim to a persistent vegetative state.

subject: BNS
question: Which one of the following Sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 prescribes punishment upto the death sentence in reference to the offence of rape ?
explanation: Section 66 of BNS prescribes punishment ranging from rigorous imprisonment of 20 years to life imprisonment or death.

subject: BNS
question: Under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 sexual intercourse by husband upon his wife during separation is punishable under :-
explanation: Section 67 of BNS penalizes non-consensual sexual intercourse by a husband upon his wife during separation under a decree or legal sanction.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' has sexual intercourse with his own wife who is living separately from him under a decree of separation without her consent. Which section of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 covers this matter?
explanation: Section 67 specifically penalizes sexual intercourse by a husband with his separated wife without her consent.

subject: BNS
question: A and B were married in the year 2015. They had one child. After living together for a few years, in January 2021, they decided to separate. No formal proceedings were initiated in a court of law, and A and B decided to live apart with mutual consent. In August 2024, the birthday celebrations of the child were taking place, and after the other guests had left and after consuming alcohol, B had sexual intercourse with his wife A, without her consent. It is important to remember that both A and B had consumed alcohol. Has B committed any offence, keeping in mind the provisions relating to sexual offences ?
options: B has committed an offence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
B has not committed an offence, however the actions of B would be an offence only If A and B were living separately under a decree of separation from a court of law.
B has not committed an offence, however the actions of B would have been an offence if A and B had obtained a decree from a court of law.
B has not committed an offence, since both A and B had consumed alcohol. However the actions of B would have been an offence is A had not consumed alcohol.
explanation: Under Section 67 of BNS, non-consensual sexual intercourse during separation (whether under a decree or custom/agreement) is punishable.

subject: BNS
question: Section 69 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 provides for :-
options: Sexual intercourse by employing deceitful means, etc.
explanation: Section 69 is a newly added provision in BNS that criminalizes obtaining sexual intercourse by false promises of marriage, employment, or deceitful identity.

subject: BNS
question: Whoever, by deceitful means or by making promise to marry to a woman without any intention of fulfilling the same, has sexual intercourse with her, such sexual intercourse not amounting to the offence of rape, shall be punished with :-
options: imprisonment which may extend to 7 years and fine
imprisonment which may extend to 10 years and fine
imprisonment which may extend to 20 years and fine
imprisonment which may extend to 10 years or imprisonment for life and fine
explanation: Section 69 of BNS provides punishment with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 10 years, along with a fine.

subject: BNS
question: "Deceitful means" under Section 69 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 shall include :-
explanation: Explanation to Section 69 defines 'deceitful means' to include false promises of employment, promotion, inducement, or marrying after suppressing identity.

subject: BNS
question: Under which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, Gang rape is punishable?
explanation: Section 70 of BNS defines and punishes the offence of gang rape.

subject: BNS
question: For 'Gang rape':-
options: It is necessary that rape should be committed by more than one person
It is committed by more than two persons
It is necessary that rape should be committed by at least five persons
None of the above is correct
explanation: Gang rape under Section 70 BNS requires two or more persons acting in furtherance of a common intention.

subject: BNS
question: In Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 the punishment for the offence of gang rape is provided :-
options: U/S 64(2)(g) minimum 10 years imprisonment but may be for life and also with fine.
U/S 64(2)(g) minimum 7 years imprisonment but may be for life and also with fine.
U/S 70(1) minimum 20 years imprisonment but may be for life and also with fine.
U/S 70(1) minimum 20 years imprisonment but which may extend to life which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life and with fine.
explanation: Section 70(1) prescribes a minimum sentence of 20 years, extending to remainder of natural life, along with a mandatory fine.

subject: BNS
question: The punishment for 'Gang Rape' as provided under Section 70(1) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is:-
options: Rigorous imprisonment which will be not less than 20 years but it may be extended upto life imprisonment which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life and with fine
Rigorous imprisonment which will be not less than 10 years but it may extended upto life imprisonment
explanation: Section 70(1) dictates rigorous imprisonment of not less than 20 years up to life (natural life) and fine.

subject: BNS
question: Maximum Punishment for Gang-Rape under 70(1) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is:-
options: Imprisonment for life which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life.
explanation: Section 70(1) caps the maximum punishment at natural life imprisonment (capital punishment applies to minor victims under Section 70(2)).

subject: BNS
question: Section 70(2) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 provides for :-
options: punishment for gang rape on woman under twelve years of age
punishment for gang rape on woman under sixteen years of age
punishment for gang rape on woman under eighteen years of age
punishment for causing death or resulting in persistent vegetative state of victim
explanation: Section 70(2) covers gang rape committed on a woman under 18 years of age.

subject: BNS
question: What is the minimum punishment for gang rape on woman under eighteen years of age under Section 70(2) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
options: rigorous imprisonment for twenty years and fine
rigorous imprisonment for fifteen yeas and fine
rigorous imprisonment for ten years and fine
imprisonment for life which, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life and fine
explanation: Section 70(2) sets the minimum punishment at natural life imprisonment with fine.

subject: BNS
question: What is the maximum punishment for gang rape on woman under eighteen years of age under Section 70(2) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
options: rigorous imprisonment for twenty years and fine
rigorous imprisonment for fifteen yeas and fine
imprisonment for life which, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life and fine
explanation: For gang rape of a victim under 18 years, Section 70(2) permits imposition of the death sentence as maximum punishment.

subject: BNS
question: Whoever, commits rape on a woman under eighteen years of age shall be punished :
options: with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than twenty years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life, and shall also be liable to fine

with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life, and shall also be liable to fine

with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than fifteen years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life, and shall also be liable to fine
with imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life, and with fine or with death
explanation: Section 65(1) read with Section 70(2) provides natural life imprisonment or death for offenses against minors under 18.

subject: BNS
question: If a person is previously convicted of an offence punishable under Section 64 or Section 65 or Section 66 or Section 70 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and is subsequently convicted for the same offence, he shall be punished under which one of the following sections ?
explanation: Section 71 of BNS (Old IPC Section 376E) covers enhanced penalties for repeat offenders.

subject: BNS
question: A who was previously convicted under section 64 Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and is again convicted under same section for life imprisonment. Here imprisonment for life means:
explanation: Repeat offenders under Section 71 receive life imprisonment defined as the remainder of that person's natural life, or death.

subject: BNS
question: Any offender, who has been previously convicted of an offence punishable under Section 64 or Section 65 or Section 66 or Section 70 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and is subsequently convicted of an offence punishable under any of the said sections shall be punished :
options: with imprisonment for life which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life or with death.
with rigorous imprisonment either description for a term which shall not be less than 10 years but which may extend to life imprisonment.
with rigorous imprisonment either description for a term which shall not be less than 7 years but which may extend to 10 years.
with rigorous imprisonment which may extend to 10 years and with fine.
explanation: Section 71 prescribes natural life imprisonment or death penalty for repeat offenders.

subject: BNS
question: Punishment for repeat offenders for rape on woman under sixteen years of age is :-
options: rigorous imprisonment for twenty years or imprisonment for life which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life
imprisonment for life which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of that person's natural life or death
explanation: Section 71 dictates that repeat offenders across sexual assault categories receive natural life imprisonment or death.

subject: BNS
question: Which of the following provision of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 criminalizes disclosure of identity of a rape victim ?
explanation: Section 72 of BNS (Old IPC Section 228A) prohibits publishing the identity of sexual offence victims.

subject: BNS
question: If a person prints or publishes the name or any matter which may make known the identity of any person against whom an offence under sections 64, 65, 66, 67, 68, 69, 70 or 71 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is alleged or found to have been committed shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to:
explanation: Section 72 prescribes imprisonment up to two years along with a fine for unauthorized disclosure of victim identity.

subject: BNS
question: Assault in order to outrage the modesty of a woman is punishable under which Section of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:-
explanation: Section 74 of BNS (Old IPC Section 354) penalizes assault or criminal force used against a woman to outrage her modesty.

subject: BNS
question: Which one of the following sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, may apply against woman also :-
explanation: Unlike gender-specific provisions, a woman can also be prosecuted under Section 74 for outraging the modesty of another woman (State of Punjab v. Major Singh).

subject: BNS
question: 'Sexual harassment' is defined under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in which Section ?
explanation: Section 75 of BNS (Old IPC Section 354A) defines and penalizes sexual harassment.

subject: BNS
question: A demand or request for sexual favour from a woman is a punishable offence under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 under :-
explanation: Demanding or requesting sexual favours is explicitly criminalized under Section 75(1)(ii) of BNS.

subject: BNS
question: When a women was taking bath in her bathroom, 'X' captures the image in his mobile. What offence has been committed by 'X' :-
options: Insulting the modesty of a women
explanation: Capturing images of a woman engaging in a private act constitutes voyeurism under Section 77 of BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Voyeurism is defined under which Section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Section 77 of BNS defines and punishes the offence of Voyeurism (Old IPC Section 354C).

subject: BNS
question: "Voyeurism" is punishable under section.................... Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
explanation: Section 77 BNS contains penalties for voyeurism.

subject: BNS
question: The offence of voyeurism under Section 77 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is committed when :-
options: A man commits the act of physical contact and advances involving unwelcome and explicit sexual overtures.
A man makes sexually coloured remarks.
A man who monitors the use by a woman of the internet, e-mail or any other form of electronic communication.

Any man who watches, or captures the image of a woman engaging in a private act in circumstances where she would usually have the expectation of not being observed either by the perpetrator or by any other person at the behest of the perpetrator or disseminates such image.
explanation: Direct statutory definition under Section 77 of BNS.

subject: BNS
question: C, being the wife of B, has obtained a decree of separation from the competent Court but they are still living in the same premises. B subjects C to intercourse. Their neighbour A watches the act and files an FIR. Which proposition is correct in these circumstances :-
options: B is guilty of the offence punishable under Section 67, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
B is not guilty of any offence because C continues to be his legally wedded wife
A would be guilty of the offence punishable under Section 77, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
explanation: Peeping/watching a private act without consent satisfies the definition of Voyeurism under Section 77 of BNS.

subject: BNS
question: In which Section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 "stalking" of a woman by any man is punishable ?
explanation: Section 78 of BNS (Old IPC Section 354D) penalizes stalking.

subject: BNS
question: Section 78 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is related to :-
options: Disrobe a woman is public place
Touching of women with sexual intent
explanation: Section 78 deals exclusively with physical and electronic stalking.

subject: BNS
question: A man who monitors the use by a woman of internet, e-mail or any form of electronic communication, commits the offence of:
explanation: Electronic monitoring of a woman's internet/email/communication is explicitly defined as cyber-stalking under Section 78(1)(ii) of BNS.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' & 'B' are good friends; 'A' proposes 'B' for marriage, but she denies. 'A', in suspicion of 'B's love affair with someone else, monitored her Mobile Phone and e-mail account used by 'B'. What offence has been committed by 'A'?
explanation: Monitoring mobile phones and email accounts of a woman constitutes stalking under Section 78 of BNS.

subject: BNS
question: According to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, any man who monitors the use by a woman of the internet, e-mail or any other form of electronic communication commits the offence of:-
explanation: Electronic surveillance of a female user without authorization constitutes stalking under Section 78 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Which of the following acts will amount to an offence of 'Stalking'?
options: A post graduate student walking behind a female teacher.
A police officer following a woman for detection of crime.
A male colleague monitoring the e-mails of female colleague.
explanation: Monitoring emails satisfies the electronic monitoring branch of stalking under Section 78 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Even after clear indication of disinterest shown by a woman to man, if such man follows her, then under which circumstance it would not constitute offence of stalking?"
options: It was pursued under a law
explanation: Exception to Section 78 BNS protects acts pursued for the purpose of preventing or detecting crime by a person entrusted with statutory duty.

subject: BNS
question: Offence of 'stalking' will be complete when :-
options: a man walks behind a group of young and old women
a man watches or captures the image of a woman engaging in private act
a man does an act to disrobe a woman
explanation: Stalking requires following/contacting despite disinterest or electronic monitoring; none of options (a), (b), or (c) fit the complete statutory criteria of Section 78 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: A man who regularly visits the instagram page of a bikini model women celebrity and also follows her, commits the offence of :-
explanation: Viewing public social media profiles created by celebrities does not satisfy the requirements of non-consensual tracking or intrusion under Section 78 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: A young man waves a currency note of rupees two thousand in front of a woman as if he offer the money for an indecent favour from the woman, he may be criminally booked under :-
explanation: Section 79 of BNS (Old IPC Section 509) penalizes words, gestures, or acts intended to insult the modesty of a woman.

subject: BNS
question: "Dowry Death" is an offence under :-
explanation: Dowry death is penalized under Section 80 of BNS (Old IPC Section 304B).

subject: BNS
question: Bride burning is an offence as defined under :-
explanation: Unnatural deaths by burning or injury connected to dowry harassment are covered under Section 80 of BNS.

subject: BNS
question: A necessary ingredient for the charge of Section 80, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is that death should occur otherwise than under normal circumstances within..............of marriage.
explanation: Section 80 of BNS specifies that the death must take place within seven years of marriage.

subject: BNS
question: The offence of dowry death under Section 80 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is committed where the death of a woman is caused by any burns or bodily injury or occurs otherwise than under normal circumstances within :-
options: seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband.

ten years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry.

seven years of her marriage and it is shown that soon before her death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry.
seven years of her marriage and it is shown that she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of her husband for, or in connection with, any demand for dowry.
explanation: Direct statutory text from Section 80(1) BNS requiring: death within 7 years, unnatural circumstances, and cruelty/harassment soon before death related to dowry demands.

subject: BNS
question: Which is not the ingredient of offence of Dowry Death defined under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:-
options: Women was subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or by any other person.
Cruelty or harassment with women should be in connection with demand for dowry.
explanation: Cruelty must be committed by the husband or his relatives, not by 'any other person' generally.

subject: BNS
question: Which is not the essential ingredient of offence of 'Dowry Death' :
options: Cruelty or harassment towards woman by her husband or any relative of her husband for or in connection or with any demand of dowry
Cruelty must be soon before her death
Ocular testimony regarding injuries by accused person to woman
Death of woman within seven years of her marriage
explanation: Direct ocular testimony is not mandatory; presumption under Evidence Act/BSA applies upon establishing basic facts.

subject: BNS
question: Wife of 'A', committed suicide after 2 years of her marriage and before her death she was subjected to cruelty and harassment by 'A' and his parents for demand of dowry. 'A' and his parents have committed offence :-
explanation: Unnatural death (suicide) within 7 years linked with dowry cruelty constitutes Dowry Death under Section 80 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Which punishment is prescribed under section 80 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
options: Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life.
Imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life and fine.
Death or imprisonment for life and fine.
Imprisonment for life or imprisonment for ten years and fine.
explanation: Section 80(2) specifies minimum 7 years imprisonment up to life imprisonment.

subject: BNS
question: A man by deceit caused a woman, not lawfully married to him, to believe that she is lawfully married to him and to cohabit with him in that belief, is dealt under section............of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
explanation: Section 81 of BNS (Old IPC Section 493) penalizes deceitfully inducing cohabitation by creating a belief of lawful marriage.

subject: BNS
question: Who may complain for 'Bigamy' under Section 82, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
options: Mother, Father, Brother or Sister on behalf of wife
explanation: Under procedural provisions governing bigamy, specified close relatives (father, mother, brother, sister) can lodge complaints on behalf of an aggrieved wife.

subject: BNS
question: In which of the following offences criminal intention (Mens-rea) is irrelevant ?
explanation: Bigamy is a statutory offence where mens rea is generally excluded once the second marriage during the subsistence of a valid first marriage is established.

subject: BNS
question: The law of bigamy does not apply where :-
options: The other spouse was living in a shared house
Bonafide reasons to believe that spouse was dead
explanation: Exception to Section 82 BNS excludes cases where a spouse has been continuously absent for seven years and not heard of, creating a bona fide belief of death.

subject: BNS
question: Sarla Mudgal, President Kalyani Vs. Union of India is a case on which one of the following?
explanation: Sarla Mudgal v. Union of India (1995) is a landmark case holding that conversion to another religion does not automatically dissolve a Hindu marriage to validate a second marriage.

subject: BNS
question: A Hindu husband converting to Islam and marrying again will be guilty of bigamy. It was held in which of the following case?
options: Sarla Mudgal v. Union of India
explanation: Sarla Mudgal v. Union of India affirmed that a second marriage by a converted husband remains bigamous under penal law.

subject: BNS
question: Which of the following cases is not related to 'bigamy'?
explanation: R v. Tolson, R v. Wheat, and R v. Dolman are leading English decisions on bigamy and mistake of fact, whereas State of U.P. v. Premi does not relate to bigamy.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' entices away 'B's wife from the house of 'B'. 'A' has committed the offence under :-
explanation: Section 84 of BNS (Old IPC Section 498) punishes enticing or taking away or detaining a married woman with criminal intent.

subject: BNS
question: Section 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is related with :-
options: Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty
explanation: Section 85 of BNS (Old IPC Section 498A) penalizes cruelty inflicted by a husband or his relatives.

subject: BNS
question: The offence of cruelty in Section 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 punishes subjecting a woman to cruelty by :-
options: the husband or relative of the husband of a woman
any person known to the woman
explanation: The offence under Section 85 specifically lies against the husband or relatives of the husband.

subject: BNS
question: Which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 provides for punishment for subjecting women to cruelty?
explanation: Section 85 prescribes the punishment of imprisonment up to three years and fine for cruelty.

subject: BNS
question: The punishment for the harassment of the woman by her husband or any of his relatives with a view to coercing her or any person related to her for dowry is imprisonment for a term which may extend upto :-
explanation: Section 85 BNS sets the maximum term of imprisonment at three years along with fine.

subject: BNS
question: Cognizance of an offence under Section 85 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 can be taken by a Court :-
options: on the complaint of the person aggrieved
on the complaint of father/mother of the person aggrieved
explanation: Procedural laws permit courts to take cognizance via police report or direct complaint by the aggrieved woman or her parents/relatives.

subject: BNS
question: Which one of the following cases pertains to the misuse of Section 498A, IPC [Now, Section 85 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023]?
options: Naresh Kumar v. State of Himachal Pradesh, AIR 2017 SC 3859
Preeti Gupta v. State of Jharkhand, AIR 2010 SC 3363
Rajendra Paswan v. State of Jharkhand & Others, AIR 2017 Jhar. 123
Z v. State of Bihar, AIR 2017 SC 3908
explanation: In Preeti Gupta v. State of Jharkhand, the Supreme Court highlighted concerns regarding the implications and misuse of Section 498A IPC against distant relatives.

subject: BNS
question: In which case Supreme Court has observed that in some circumstances evidence of a deceased wife with respect to cruelty could be admissible in a trial for a charge under Section 498-A of the IPC under Section 32(1) of the Evidence Act [Now, Section 85 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 and Section 26(a) of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023].........as long as the cause of her death has come into question whether the charge relating to death is proved or not is immaterial with respect to admissibility.
options: Surendran Vs. State of Kerala, 2022 SCC Online SC 621
Kumar Ghimirey Vs. State of Sikkim, AIR 2019 SC 2011
Sunil Kumar Vs. State of Kerala and another, AIR 2022 SC 3007
Rajesh alias Sarkari and another Vs. State of Haryana, AIR 2020 SC 5561
explanation: Surendran v. State of Kerala (2022) addressed the admissibility of dying declarations under Evidence Act provisions relating to charges of marital cruelty.

subject: BNS
question: Cruelty to a woman by husband or relative of husband is defined under :-
options: Section 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Section 84 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Section 83 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Section 86 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
explanation: Section 86 of BNS contains the specific definition of 'cruelty' (previously embedded in the Explanation to IPC Section 498A).

subject: BNS
question: Cruelty under section 85 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 includes:-
options: wilful conduct likely to drive the women to commit suicide
wilful conduct likely to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health
harassment with a view to coerce her to meet any unlawful demand of dowry
explanation: Section 86 BNS includes physical/mental harm, driving to suicide, and unlawful dowry coercion within the ambit of cruelty.

subject: BNS
question: 'X' with the intention to cause miscarriage, administered a drug to a pregnant lady 'Y'. The child in the womb died. 'X' is guilty of :-
options: culpable homicide not amounting to murder
explanation: Section 88 of BNS (Old IPC Section 312) penalizes voluntarily causing miscarriage.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' claiming to be a family planning expert gave 'X' some chemical. After consuming the chemical, the child in the womb of 'X' die in the womb. 'A' has committed :-
options: Offence of culpable homicide not amounting to murder
explanation: Administering substances to terminate a fetus outside medical exceptions constitutes the offence of causing miscarriage under Section 88 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Death caused by an act done with intent to cause miscarriage is dealt with under :-
explanation: Section 90 of BNS (Old IPC Section 314) penalizes acts done with intent to cause miscarriage that result in the woman's death.

subject: BNS
question: 'A', knowing that he is likely to cause then death of a pregnant woman, does an act which, if it caused the death of the woman, would amount to culpable homicide. The woman does not die but the death of an unborn quick child with which she is pregnant is thereby caused. 'A' is guilty of the offence defined in the :-
explanation: Section 92 of BNS (Old IPC Section 316) governs causing the death of a quick unborn child by an act amounting to culpable homicide.

subject: BNS
question: "A" with intention of causing the death of a child "B" who is below 12 years, exposes him in a desert place. Here "A" will be liable under which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:-
explanation: Section 93 of BNS (Old IPC Section 317) penalizes the exposure and abandonment of a child under twelve years by parents or caretakers.

subject: BNS
question: Section 93 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 punishes the offence of exposure and abandonment of a child under 12 years by parent or person having care of it. Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 provides for punishment for the offence of culpable homicide not amounting to murder. 'A' exposes her child with the knowledge that she is thereby likely to cause its death. The child dies in consequence of such exposure. In such circumstances 'A' may be :-
options: charged with and convicted of the offence under Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
charged with and convicted of the offences under Sections 93 and 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
charged with and convicted of the offence under Section 93 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
charged with the offences under Sections 93 and 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 but convicted only for the offence under Section 105
explanation: Exposure of a child resulting in death supports charges and convictions for both abandonment (Section 93) and culpable homicide (Section 105) per Explanation to Section 93 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: A and B being the parents of infant X, abandon the infant in the middle of the night during the winter season. As a result, the X suffers from the hypothermia. X is discovered by a good Samaritan who rushes X to the hospital. Unfortunately, the facilities at the hospital were inadequate and X dies. During the course of the investigation, it is also revealed that the X may have survived if X had received appropriate medical care at the hospital. In these circumstances, offences under which provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 have been committed by A and B ?
explanation: Parents abandoning an infant exposed to lethal weather commit abandonment (Section 93) and murder/culpable homicide (Section 103) as the causal chain remains unbroken by medical inadequacies.

subject: BNS
question: Under Section 95 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 which of the following offence is punishable :-
options: Hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence
Hiring, employing or engaging a woman to commit an offence
Hiring, employing or engaging any person to commit an offence
explanation: Section 95 is a newly inserted provision in BNS that explicitly criminalizes hiring, employing, or engaging children to commit crimes.

subject: BNS
question: Whoever hires, employs or engages any child to commit an offence shall be punished with imprisonment of either description :-
options: which shall not be less than 3 years but which may extend to 5 years, and with fine
which shall not be less than 3 years but which may extend to 10 years, and with fine
which shall not be less than 5 years but which may extend to 10 years, and with fine
which shall not be less than 7 years but which may extend to 10 years, and with fine
explanation: Section 95 BNS mandates imprisonment of not less than 3 years, extendable to 10 years, and fine.

subject: BNS
question: Whoever kidnaps or abducts any child with intention of taking dishonestly any movable property from the person of such child, shall be punished under Section 97 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 if the child is under :-
explanation: Section 97 of BNS (Old IPC Section 369) applies specifically to children under ten years of age.

subject: BNS
question: Offences against human body are provided under which of the following chapters of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 :-
explanation: Under BNS, offences affecting the human body are compiled in Chapter VI (Sections 100 to 146).

subject: BNS
question: Which of the following provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 defines culpable homicide?
explanation: Section 100 of BNS defines culpable homicide (replacing Old IPC Section 299).

subject: BNS
question: Acts which come in the category of 'culpable homicide not amounting to murder' are mentioned in which section of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Section 100 of BNS defines culpable homicide. Section 101 specifies when culpable homicide constitutes murder; acts that do not satisfy those criteria or fall under its exceptions remain culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

subject: BNS
question: Whoever causes death by doing an act with the intention of causing death or with the intention of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death or with the knowledge that he is likely by such act to cause death, commits the offence of :-
explanation: Direct definition of Culpable Homicide as provided under Section 100 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (replacing Old IPC Section 299).

subject: BNS
question: Culpable homicide means :-
options: causing injury which is likely to cause death
explanation: Culpable homicide fundamentally means human killing done with the mental element (mens rea) of intending death or knowing that death is likely to follow.

subject: BNS
question: 'A culpable homicide is the genus, and murder its species'. The statement is :-
explanation: As laid down by Melvill, J. in the classic case of Reg v. Govinda, all murders are culpable homicides, but all culpable homicides are not murders; hence culpable homicide is the genus and murder is the species.

subject: BNS
question:
Assertion (A): Homicide is the killing of a human being by a human being.
Reason (R): Homicide is always unlawful.

Select the correct answer with the help of codes given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Homicide is the killing of a human being by another human being, but it is not always unlawful (e.g., lawful/justifiable homicide committed in self-defence, execution of legal sentence, or by accident).

subject: BNS
question: Which one of the following option is incorrect?
options: All Murders are culpable homicide but not vice versa.
An intention to kill is not always necessary to make out a case of murder.
Clause (c) of Section 100 requires knowledge of the probability of death
explanation: Statement (b) is incorrect because culpable homicide is the broader category (genus), and only specific aggravated forms of culpable homicide qualify as murder under Section 101 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: The mens rea required under Section 100 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is :-
explanation: Section 100 BNS explicitly requires either the intention to cause death/bodily injury likely to cause death, or the knowledge that the act is likely to cause death.

subject: BNS
question: Culpable homicide is causing death :-
options: with the intention of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death
with the knowledge that by such act death is likely to be caused
with the intention of causing death
explanation: Section 100 of BNS lists all three ingredients in clauses (a), (b), and (c) as constituent elements of culpable homicide.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' with intention to facilitate robbery put a residential house to fire in the night & causes death of a person due to this fire. 'A' has committed the offence of :-
options: only for putting fire in a house
explanation: Setting fire to an occupied dwelling house carries the knowledge that death is likely to be caused, satisfying Section 100 BNS for culpable homicide.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' lays sticks and turf over a pit, with the intention thereby causing death. 'Z' believing the ground to be firm, treads on it, falls in and is killed. 'A' is guilty of :-
explanation: Standard statutory illustration to Section 100 BNS (Old IPC Section 299 Illustration a).

subject: BNS
question: 'X' knows 'Z' to be behind a bush. 'Y' does not know about it. 'X', intending to cause or knowing it to be likely to cause 'Z's death, induces 'Y' to fire at the bush. 'Y' fires and Kills 'Z'. What is the guilt of 'X' and 'Y'?
options: Both X and Y are guilty of having committed culpable of homicide
Both X and Y are guilty of having committed murder
X is guilty of having committed culpable homicide but Y is not guilty of having committed any offence, whatsoever
X is guilty of having committed murder, but Y is not guilty of having committed any offence.
explanation: Statutory illustration to Section 100 BNS (Old IPC Section 299 Illustration b). Y acts innocently without mens rea, while X possesses the required intention/knowledge.

subject: BNS
question: A knows Z to be behind a bush. B does not know it, A, intending to cause, or knowing it to be likely to cause Z's death, induces B to fire at the bush. B fires and kills Z. Here B may be guilty of no offence, but A has committed the offence of :-
explanation: Direct application of Illustration (b) to Section 100 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: 'J', a priest, beats a boy for curing him from evil spirit. The boy dies 'J' is :-
options: Entitled to the defence of good faith
explanation: Severely beating a child to exorcise spirits, knowing that such severe physical harm is likely to cause death, removes good faith and constitutes culpable homicide.

subject: BNS
question: Causing of the death of child in mother's womb is :-
explanation: Under Explanation 3 to Section 100 BNS, causing the death of a child in the mother's womb is not homicide (it is punishable separately under Section 88/92 BNS).

subject: BNS
question: Causing death to a child in a mother's womb is not homicide. It is provided under :-
options: Explanation-I to Section 100, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Explanation-II to Section 100, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Explanation-III to Secton 100, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Explanation-V to Section 101, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
explanation: Explanation 3 to Section 100 BNS explicitly states that causing the death of a child in the mother's womb is not homicide.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' beat his wife, she fell down and becomes unconscious. Believing her to be dead and to save himself from being arrested for murder, 'A' hanged her in fan with rope. Post mortem disclosed her death from hanging, 'A' is liable for ?
explanation: Based on Palani Goundan v. Emperor / In re Thavamani, where the accused acts under the belief that the victim is already dead, the acts form part of a single transaction amounting to culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

subject: BNS
question: In Reg v Govinda the points of distinction between the provisions of the following sections of the IPC were explained :-
options: 34 and 149 [Now, Sections 3(5) and 190 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023]
302 and 304 [Now, Sections 103 and 105 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023]
299 and 300 [Now, Sections 100 and 101 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023]
403 and 405 [Now, Sections 314 and 316(1) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023]
explanation: Melvill, J. in Reg v. Govinda (1876) laid down the classic comparative framework between Culpable Homicide (Section 299 IPC / Section 100 BNS) and Murder (Section 300 IPC / Section 101 BNS).

subject: BNS
question: The distinction between section 299 and section 300 of IPC, 1860 [Now, Sections 100 and 101 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023] was first elaborately discussed in the following case :-
options: Om Prakash v. State of Punjab
explanation: Reg v. Govinda is the foundational authority establishing the degree of probability of death that separates culpable homicide from murder.

subject: BNS
question: Under which one of the following cases, first time, the Supreme Court of India, has reaffirmed the distinction between culpable homicide and murder while adopting the view suggested in Govind case :-
options: Inder Singh v. State of PEPSU
State of A.P. v. R.R. Punnayya
K.M. Nanawati v. State of Maharashtra
explanation: In State of A.P. v. R.R. Punnayya (1977), the Supreme Court structured the scheme of IPC/BNS into three stages following the principles of Reg v. Govinda.

subject: BNS
question: In which of the following leading cases, Justice Vivian Bose distinguished culpable homicide and murder?
options: Virsa Singh v. State of Punjab, AIR 1958 SC 465
Shivaji Sahabrao Bobode v. State of Maharashtra, AIR 1973 SC 2622
Rudul Shah v. State of Bihar, AIR 1983 SC 1086
explanation: Justice Vivian Bose in Virsa Singh v. State of Punjab (1958) formulated the four-point test for determining liability under Section 300 'Thirdly' (Section 101(c) BNS).

subject: BNS
question: State of A.P. v. R. Punnayya case deals with distinction between which of following sections of Indian Penal Code?
options: Section 501 and 502 [Now, Secs. 356(3) and 356(4) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023]
Sections 299 and 300 [Now, Secs. 100 and 101 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023]
Section 304A and 304B [Now, Secs. 106 and 80 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023]
Section 305 and 306 [Now, Secs. 107 and 108 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023]
explanation: State of A.P. v. R.R. Punnayya is a locus classicus explaining the statutory interplay between Section 299 (Culpable Homicide) and Section 300 (Murder).

subject: BNS
question: Murder is defined in the following section of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 :-
explanation: Section 101 of BNS defines murder and lists its five exceptions (replacing Old IPC Section 300).

subject: BNS
question: When the injury is intentional and sufficient to cause death in the ordinary course of nature and death follow, the offence is :-
options: culpable homicide and amounting to murder
explanation: Under Section 101(c) of BNS, causing bodily injury intended to be inflicted that is sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death constitutes murder.

subject: BNS
question: Intention to cause death is not essential under which clause of Section 101 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:-
explanation: Clause (d) of Section 101 BNS (4thly) relies entirely on the knowledge that the act is so imminently dangerous that it must in all probability cause death, without requiring direct intention to kill.

subject: BNS
question: Under Section 101 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, how many kinds of exceptions have been stipulated, where culpable homicide is not murder ?
explanation: Section 101 BNS lists 5 exceptions: Grave & Sudden Provocation, Private Defence excess, Public Servant excess, Sudden Fight, and Consent of victim above 18 years.

subject: BNS
question: The plea of "sudden and grave provocation" under Section 101 Exception (1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is a :-
options: Mixed question of law and fact
explanation: Explanation to Exception 1 of Section 101 BNS explicitly states: 'Whether the provocation was grave and sudden enough to prevent the offence from amounting to murder is a question of fact.'

subject: BNS
question: In the context of the exception of grave and sudden provocation, which of the following is correct?
options: provocation should not be voluntarily provoked by the offender
lawful exercise of the right of private defence does not give provocation
lawful exercise of power by a public servant in obedience to the law does not amount to provocation
explanation: All three conditions are express provisos restricting the availability of Exception 1 to Section 101 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Culpable Homicide is not murder if done under :
explanation: Sudden and grave provocation is Exception 1 to Section 101 BNS. Intoxication or irresistible impulse are not statutory exceptions under this section.

subject: BNS
question: Which one is incorrect ? Culpable homicide does not amount to murder in certain cases of grave and sudden provocation provided :-
options: the question whether the provocation was grave and sudden is a pure question of law
the provocation was not sought by the offender
the provocation is not given by anything done in the lawful exercise of right of private defence
the provocation is not given by anything done in obedience to law
explanation: Statement (a) is incorrect because whether provocation was grave and sudden is explicitly a question of fact, not law.

subject: BNS
question: Grave and sudden provocation is a :-
options: mixed question of law and fact
explanation: Statutorily defined as a question of fact in the Explanation to Exception 1 of Section 101 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Culpable homicide is not murder if it is committed:-
options: when the offender is acting in anger
when the offender is acting under the spell of madness
with the consent of the victim, who has completed 18 years of age.
with the consent of the victim who has completed 12 years of age
explanation: Exception 5 to Section 101 BNS provides that culpable homicide is not murder when the person whose death is caused, being above the age of 18 years, suffers death or takes the risk of death with his own consent.

subject: BNS
question: Give the correct response :-
options: An intention to kill is not always necessary to make out a case of murder
A knowledge that the natural and probable consequence of an act would be death could make out a case of murder
explanation: Murder can be established either through specific bodily injury intention or through imminent knowledge under Section 101 BNS clauses (c) and (d).

subject: BNS
question: 'A' fires a bullet into a bush, where unknown to him 'Y' is doing some work and bullet kills 'Y'. 'A' is not guilty of murder of 'Y' because 'A' had not fired intentionally at 'Y'.
explanation: In the absence of intention or knowledge regarding Y's presence, the element of mens rea for murder is completely absent.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' appears as a witness before 'Z', a magistrate, 'Z' says that he does not believe a word of A's deposition, and that 'A' has perjured himself. 'A' is moved to sudden passion by these words and kills 'Z'. This is :-
options: culpable Homicide not amounting to murder
explanation: Proviso 2 to Exception 1 of Section 101 BNS states that provocation given by anything done in obedience to law or by a public servant in lawful exercise of power does not reduce murder to culpable homicide.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' with intent to murder, administered a fatal dose of poison to 'Z', and then while 'Z' was still alive, a stranger 'B', without A's knowledge attacked 'Z' and shot him dead ?
options: 'A' and 'B' both would be guilty of murder.
'A' would be guilty of culpable homicide and 'B' would be guilty of murder
'A' would be guilty of an attempt to murder and 'B' would be guilty of murder.
'A' would be guilty of instigating 'B' to commit murder and 'B' would be guilty of murder.
explanation: The direct cause of death was B's gunshot wound, making B liable for murder. Since Z did not die from the poison, A's act remains an attempt to murder (Section 109 BNS).

subject: BNS
question: 'A' with the intention of murdering 'Z' instigates 'B' a child below seven years of age, to do an act which causes 'Z's death. 'B', in consequence of instigation, did the act in the absence of 'A' thereby causes 'Z's death. What offence has been committed by 'A'?
options: No offence, because 'A' was not present at the time of murder
Committed simple offence of causing hurt
Committed offence of attempt to murder
explanation: A person who uses an innocent agent (doli incapax child under 7) to commit a crime is treated as the principal offender and is guilty of murder under Section 101 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' snake-charmer while showing his play claims to cure the snake bite. The deceased got himself a snake bite believing on assurance of the snake-charmer. The snake-charmer could not cure the deceased. The snake-charmer is liable for:-
options: may be liable for culpable homicide
explanation: Based on Poonai Fattemah v. Emperor, exposing a person to a deadly snake bite knowing that death is the probable result constitutes murder, as consent given under misrepresentation of cure is invalid.

subject: BNS
question: 'X' drives very fast through a crowded road to catch a flight knowing that his act in "all probability" may cause death. 'Y' is killed by his vehicle. 'X' is guilty of
options: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
explanation: Under Section 101(d) BNS (4thly), committing an act so imminently dangerous that in all probability it must cause death without excuse constitutes murder.

subject: BNS
question: "A" being a medical expert blows on the head of "B", who is suffering from third stage brain cancer. Consequently "B" dies immediately on the spot. "A" knows the fact that a blow on the head of "B" can lead to death. What offence "A" has committed ?
options: Murder, as "A" knew that his act is likely to cause death of "B" to whom injury is inflicted
No offence as the blow would not have caused death of a normal man in ordinary circumstances
An offence other than murder or culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
Culpable homicide not amounting to murder as "A" knew that his act is likely to cause death.
explanation: Under Section 101(b) BNS (2ndly), if the offender knows the special bodily condition of the victim and inflicts bodily injury intending/knowing it will cause death to that specific person, it is murder.

subject: BNS
question: X knows Y is suffering from a disease in his head and a blow to Y on his head to cause his death. X gives a fist blow to Y on his head. Y died. X is guilty :-
explanation: Direct application of Section 101(b) BNS (2ndly); special knowledge of the victim's physical condition elevates culpable homicide to murder.

subject: BNS
question: 'X' and 'Y' go to murder 'Z'. 'X' stood on guard with a spear in hand but did not hit 'Z' at all. 'Y' killed 'Z':-
options: Only 'Y' is liable for murder of 'Z'
'X' and 'Y' are liable for murder of 'Z'
'X' is not liable as he did not perform overt act
explanation: Under Section 3(5) of BNS (Old IPC Section 34 - Common Intention), standing guard to facilitate murder makes X equally liable for murder with Y (Barendra Kumar Ghosh v. King Emperor).

subject: BNS
question: 'Z' strikes 'B'. 'B' is by this provocation excited to violent rage. 'A', a bystander intending to take advantage of B's rage and to cause him to kill 'Z' puts a knife into B's hand for that purpose. 'B' kills 'Z' with the knife. What offence 'A' is guilty of :-
options: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
explanation: Statutory illustration to Section 101 BNS. A acted with premeditated malice without provocation, so A is guilty of murder.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' placed a bomb in a medical store and gave the people inside three minutes time to get out before the bomb exploded. 'B' an arthritic patient, failed to escape and was killed. 'A' is liable for:-
explanation: Detonating an explosive in a store is an imminently dangerous act that in all probability causes death under Section 101(d) BNS.

subject: BNS
question: C, under the influence of passion excited by a provocation given by A intentionally kills A's child named B. C has committed an offence of :-
options: culpable homicide not amounting to murder
not committed any offence because he kills 'B' due to provocation
causes the death of 'B' by doing rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide
explanation: Exception 1 to Section 101 BNS applies only if the person killed is the one who gave the provocation. Killing an innocent third party/child remains murder.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' without any excuse fires a loaded cannon into a crowd of persons and kills one of them. Although he may not have had a premeditated design to kill any particular individual. 'A' committed offence of :-
explanation: Illustration (d) to Section 101 BNS; firing a cannon into a crowd is an act imminently dangerous to human life amounting to murder under Section 101.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' without any excuse fires a loaded cannon into a crowd of persons and kills one of them. 'A' is guilty of which one of the following offences under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:-
options: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
explanation: Direct application of Illustration (d) to Section 101 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' gave poisoned "Halwa" (sweet dish) to 'B' with intention to kill him. 'B' ate one spoon and kept it on the side. 'C' who was sitting there, picked up and ate it. 'C' dies. Here 'A' is guilty of :-
options: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
Here 'A' is not guilty of murder as he never intended to kill 'C'
explanation: Under Section 102 of BNS (Doctrine of Transferred Malice), causing the death of a person other than the intended target constitutes murder.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' intentionally cause B's death partly by illegally omitting to give 'B' food and partly by beating. 'A' has committed the offence of :-
options: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
explanation: Illustration (a) to Section 101 BNS; combining illegal omission (starvation) with overt acts (beating) to cause death constitutes murder.

subject: BNS
question: Z's actions give A circumstances of grave and sudden provocation, and A starts attacking Z. B happens to chance upon the fight, and decides to assist A in attacking Z. As a result, Z dies. Which of the following is true?
options: A and B have both committed Murder.
A has committed Murder and B has committed culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
A and B have both committed culpable homicide not amounting to murder
A has committed culpable homicide not amounting to murder, and B has committed murder.
explanation: Exception 1 of Section 101 BNS is personal to A who suffered the provocation. B, acting without provocation out of independent malice, is guilty of murder.

subject: BNS
question: A attacks Z under such circumstances of grave provocation that his killing of Z would be only culpable homicide not amounting to murder. B, having ill-will towards Z and intending to kill him, and not having been subject to the provocation, assists A in killing Z. In such circumstances which one is correct :
options: Both A and B are guilty of murder
Both A and B are guilty of Culpable Homicide
A is guilty of Culpable Homicide and B is guilty of Abetment of Murder
A is guilty of Culpable Homicide and B is guilty of Murder
explanation: Different liabilities attach to participants based on their distinct mens rea: A gets the benefit of Exception 1, while B is liable for murder.

subject: BNS
question: A, a jailor has charge of Z, a prisoner. Intending to cause his death, A illegally omits to supply Z with food. This causes Z's strength to reduce and causes him weakness. Y, a prisoner, who is unaware of his weakness, gets into a fight with Z which results in the death of Z, which may not have happened if Z was given adequate nutrition. Keeping Section 3(8) and 101 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in mind, which of the following is true?
options: A and Y have both committed murder.
A has committed attempt to murder, and Y has committed culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
A has committed attempt to murder, and Y has committed murder.
A is not guilty of any offence, Y has committed culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
explanation: Y caused death without knowledge of Z's extreme weakness (culpable homicide/voluntarily hurt), whereas A's illegal omission did not directly cause death due to the intervening act of Y, rendering A liable for attempt to murder.

subject: BNS
question: "All murder is culpable homicide but all culpable homicide is not murder." This statement has been given by:-
explanation: Historically articulated by Melvill, J. in Reg v. Govinda (1876) to define the relationship between culpable homicide and murder. (Option C maintained strictly per source key).

subject: BNS
question: Give the correct response :-
options: All murders are culpable homicide but not vice versa
A murder can never be a culpable homicide
explanation: Culpable homicide is the broader category; murder is an aggravated form of culpable homicide.

subject: BNS
question: Which one of the following option is incorrect?
options: All murders are culpable homicide but not vice versa
An intention to kill is not always necessary to make out a case of murder
Clause (c) of Section 100 require knowledge of the probability of death
explanation: Statement (b) is false as culpable homicide includes offences that do not amount to murder.

subject: BNS
question: "A" sees "B" drowning, but does not save him. "B" is drowned. "A" has committed :-
options: the offence of abetment of suicide
the offence of culpable homicide not amounting to murder
explanation: Criminal law requires a legal duty to act. A mere moral duty without a legal obligation does not create criminal liability for an omission.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' is a national champion of swimming in pond. He could have saved the child, but did not do so. The child drowned. Is 'A' guilty of:-
options: culpable homicide not amounting to murder
explanation: Omission to act without a legal duty to rescue does not constitute an offence under penal law.

subject: BNS
question: Which one of the following is not punishable under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
options: Preparation to wage war against the State
Preparation to commit depredation on the territory of a friendly power
explanation: Preparation is generally not punishable under penal law except for specified offences (e.g., waging war, dacoity, depredation). Preparation to commit murder is not penalized.

subject: BNS
question: Difference between murder and culpable homicide was laid down in the case of :
options: Bachan Singh vs. State of Punjab
K.M. Nanawati vs. State of Maharashtra
explanation: Reg v. Govinda (1876) established the distinction based on degrees of probability of death.

subject: BNS
question: K.M. Nanavati Vs. State of Maharashtra is a leading case on :-
explanation: K.M. Nanavati v. State of Maharashtra (AIR 1962 SC 605) laid down guidelines for applying Exception 1 (Grave and Sudden Provocation).

subject: BNS
question: Which of the following cases is considered as locus classicus on Section 300 thirdly of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 [Now, Clause (c) of Section 101 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023]?
options: Shivaji Sahabrao Bobade v. State of Maharashtra
Virsa Singh v. State of Punjab
Rudal Shah v. State of Bihar
explanation: Virsa Singh v. State of Punjab (AIR 1958 SC 465) is the authoritative decision defining 'bodily injury sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death.'

subject: BNS
question: In which of the following landmark case, a three Judges' Bench of the Supreme Court prescribed four point test relating to Section 300, thirdly, of I.P.C. [Now, Clause (c) of Section 101 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023] :-
options: Virsa Singh vs. State of Punjab; AIR 1958 SC 465.
State of U.P. vs. Ramesh Prasad Misra; (1996) 10 SCC 360.
K.M. Nanavati vs. State of Maharashtra; AIR 1962 SC 605.
Nehru @ Jawahar vs. State AIR 2008 SC 2574
explanation: Justice Vivian Bose in Virsa Singh v. State of Punjab formulated the 4-step test for establishing murder under Clause 3rdly.

subject: BNS
question:
Match List I (Case) with List II (Subject) and select the correct answer using the Code given below the Lists :-
List I:
A. K.M. Nanavati v. State of Maharashtra
B. Virsa Singh v. State of Punjab
C. Barendra Kumar Ghosh v. Emperor
D. Shyam Behari v. State of U.P.

List II:
1. Common Intention
2. Dacoity
3. Murder
4. Grave and sudden provocation
5. Unsoundness of mind
explanation: Nanavati = Provocation (4); Virsa Singh = Murder/3rdly (3); Barendra Kumar Ghosh = Common Intention (1); Shyam Behari = Dacoity (2).

subject: BNS
question: It embodies what the English authors describe as the doctrine of transferred malice.
explanation: Section 102 of BNS (Old IPC Section 301) incorporates the doctrine of transferred malice.

subject: BNS
question: 'X' intended to kill 'A' but instead killed 'B' whom he had no intention to kill. Under which doctrine is 'X' liable for the murder of 'B' ?
explanation: Under the Doctrine of Transfer of Malice (Section 102 BNS), intention to kill one individual transfers to any unintended victim killed as a result.

subject: BNS
question: Accused aimed at 'S' but shot fired by him accidently hit 'J' and caused her death. Doctrine of "transferred malice" :-
options: is not applicable as it is a case under Section 106 i.e. causing death by negligence
explanation: Transferred malice directly applies when an intentional shot aimed at one person hits and kills another.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' intentionally fired a shot from his pistol at 'B' but it hit 'C' and 'C' died. The offence committed by 'A' is :-
explanation: Section 102 of BNS explicitly prescribes that the offender is punishable for murder as if he had caused the death of the person he intended to kill.

subject: BNS
question: "A" gave poisoned "halwa" (sweet dish) to "B" with intention to kill him. "B" ate one spoon and kept it on the side. "C" who was sitting there, picked up and ate it. "C" dies. Here "A" is guilty of :-
options: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
Here "A" is not guilty of murder as he never intended to kill "C"
explanation: Application of Section 102 BNS (Transferred Malice); intention to poison B attaches to C's death.

subject: BNS
question: 'X' threatens 'Y' that if 'Y' does not shoot 'P', 'X' will shoot 'Y'. On this, 'Y' shoots 'P' and 'P' dies. The act of 'Y' comes under :-
explanation: Compulsion by threat of death does not excuse murder under general exception provisions (Section 32 BNS); Y remains liable for murder under Section 103 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' kills 'C' thinking 'C' as 'B'. 'A' is guilty of offence punishable under :-
explanation: Mistake of identity does not negate murder liability; killing C believing him to be B is murder punishable under Section 103 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: A knows Z to be behind a bush. B does not know it. A, intending to cause, or knowing it to be likely to cause Z's death, induces B to fire at the bust. B fires and kills Z. What offence has been committed by A and B ?
options: A and B both would be guilty of committing offence punishable under Section 103, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
While A would be guilty of committing offence under Section 103, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, B would be guilty of committing offence under Section 105
A would be guilty of committing offence punishable under Section 103, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, B would be guilty of no offence
A and B both would be guilty of committing offence punishable under Section 105, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
explanation: B lacks mens rea and is innocent, while A is liable for culpable homicide/murder punishable under Section 103 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Offence of mob lynching is punishable under which Section of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 ?
explanation: Section 103(2) is a newly added provision in BNS specifically penalizing murder committed by a group/mob acting on grounds of race, caste, community, sex, place of birth, language, or personal belief.

subject: BNS
question: Minimum number of persons required for committing offence punishable under Section 103(2) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is :-
explanation: Section 103(2) BNS defines mob lynching as an offence committed by a group of five or more persons acting in concert.

subject: BNS
question: Punishment for mob lynching under Section 103(2) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is:-
options: imprisonment which may extend to 7 years or imprisonment for life and fine
imprisonment which may extend to 10 years or imprisonment for life and fine
death or imprisonment for life and fine
explanation: Section 103(2) of BNS prescribes punishment of death or imprisonment for life, along with a mandatory fine.

subject: BNS
question: The case of Bachan Singh v State of Punjab is concerned with :-
explanation: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab (1980) established the constitutional validity of capital punishment in India.

subject: BNS
question: "Death sentence should be awarded in rarest of rare cases" was held in :-
options: Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab
T.V. Vatheeswaran v. State of Tamil Nadu
State of U.P. v. M.K. Anthony
explanation: The Supreme Court in Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab laid down the 'rarest of rare cases' doctrine for awarding the death penalty.

subject: BNS
question: The case of Virsa Singh Vs. State of Punjab, 1958 SCC Online SC 37 is related with which offence ?
explanation: Virsa Singh v. State of Punjab is the benchmark judgment interpreting Section 300(3) IPC / Section 101(c) BNS regarding murder by intentional bodily injury.

subject: BNS
question: X murdered A, and was sentenced to life imprisonment. While serving his sentence, X murdered another inmate B. What punishment must follow for his action?
options: X must be punished with death
X may be sentenced to life imprisonment for remainder of his natural life or death
X cannot be punished with death, and can only be sentenced to life imprisonment
Murder of a criminal is not an offence
explanation: Mandatory death penalty under Old IPC Section 303 was struck down in Mithu v. State of Punjab. Under Section 104 BNS, punishment choices are life imprisonment or death. (Option C maintained strictly per source key).

subject: BNS
question: Not being armed with any deadly weapon and not expressing any intention to kill, A tied B to an electric pole with ropes and assaulted him as a result of which B died, A committed offence punishable under Section :-
explanation: Assaulting without intent to kill but with knowledge that bodily injury is likely to cause death constitutes culpable homicide not amounting to murder under Section 105 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: The accused inflicted injuries on non vital parts of the deceased which were not found to be sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death but it was proved that he inflicted the injuries with a knowledge that with these injuries the victim was likely to die. The case would be punishable under section :-
explanation: Section 105 Part II applies when an act is done with knowledge that it is likely to cause death, but without intention to cause death or fatal bodily injury.

subject: BNS
question: The culpable homicide not amounting to murder is committed with the knowledge that it is likely to cause death, but without any intention to cause death, or to cause such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, is punishable :-
options: under Section 105 part-I and with life imprisonment
under Section 105 part-II and only with the maximum imprisonment for a term of 14 years
under Section 105 part-II and with imprisonment for a term which may extend to 10 years and fine.
explanation: Section 105 Part II BNS prescribes imprisonment up to 10 years, or fine, or both for acts done with knowledge only.

subject: BNS
question: Section 93 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 punishes the offence of exposure and abandonment of a child under 12 years by parent or person having care of it. Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 provides for punishment for the offence of culpable homicide not amounting to murder. 'A' exposes her child with the knowledge that she is thereby likely to cause its death. The child dies in consequence of such exposure. In such circumstances 'A' may be :-
options: charged with and convicted of the offence under Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
charged with and convicted of the offences under Sections 93 and 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
charged with and convicted of the offence under Section 93 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
charged with the offences under Sections 93 and 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 but convicted only for the offence under Section 105
explanation: Under Explanation to Section 93 BNS, charging and convicting for both child abandonment (Section 93) and culpable homicide (Section 105) is statutorily permitted if death occurs.

subject: BNS
question: Death caused by rash and negligent act is covered in Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 under :-
explanation: Section 106 of BNS (Old IPC Section 304A) governs causing death by rash or negligent act.

subject: BNS
question: Section 106 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 pertains to :-
options: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder
explanation: Section 106 contains provisions for causing death by medical negligence, rash driving, and hit-and-run incidents.

subject: BNS
question: Which one of the following offences is bailable?
options: murder under Section 103, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
death by negligence under Section 106(1), Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
dowry death under Section 80, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
abetment to commit suicide under Section 108, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
explanation: Causing death by negligence under Section 106(1) BNS is a bailable offence under procedural law schedules.

subject: BNS
question: If in a trial for 'causing death by negligence' it is established that the accused had been at fault though victim had also been equally at fault :-
options: the fact that the actual injury was brought about by carelessness or contribution of the victim also, will be no defence
contributory negligence would be a good defence
the degree of culpability as to the amount of negligence on his part shall be deciding factor
