explanation: Contributory negligence of the victim is not a complete defence in criminal law; the court evaluates whether the accused's gross negligence was the direct and proximate cause of death.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' is cutting the wood with an axe at a place where children are playing. The axe flies off and kills a nearby child. 'A' is liable for :-
explanation: Cutting wood near playing children without taking reasonable care/caution lacks proper care, constituting criminal negligence under Section 106(1) BNS.

subject: BNS
question: The maximum term of imprisonment which can be imposed by the court for the offence under Section 106(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is :-
explanation: Section 106(1) of BNS increased the general penalty for causing death by negligence up to five years (previously two years under IPC Section 304A).

subject: BNS
question: The punishment for causing death by negligence by registered medical practitioner u/s. 106(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is :-
options: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years and fine
imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years and fine
imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and fine
imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years and fine
explanation: Proviso to Section 106(1) BNS retains a specific 2-year imprisonment cap for registered medical practitioners performing medical procedures.

subject: BNS
question: Hit and run motor accident is punishable under which of the following Section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:-
explanation: Section 106(2) of BNS specifically punishes hit-and-run incidents where an offender escapes without reporting to a police officer or magistrate.

subject: BNS
question: The maximum punishment for hit and run prescribed under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita is:-
explanation: Section 106(2) of BNS provides imprisonment for a term which may extend to 10 years and fine for hit-and-run offences.

subject: BNS
question: Which of the following provision of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is excluded from enforcement from 1st July, 2024 :-
options: the provision of sub-section (1) of section 106
the provision of sub-section (2) of section 106
the provision of sub-section (1) of section 108
the provision of sub-section (2) of section 108
explanation: Section 106(2) BNS (Hit and Run provision) was kept in abeyance and excluded from the operational notification when BNS came into force on July 1, 2024.

subject: BNS
question: Every doctor is not responsible under Section 304 (A) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 [Now, Section 106(1) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023], for death of a person due to his negligent operation unless his intention is culpable. This has been laid down in :-
options: Sarvenvar Parsad Sharma v. State, 1978 SC
Jacob Mathew v. State of Punjab, 2005 SC
explanation: In Jacob Mathew v. State of Punjab (2005), the Supreme Court ruled that gross negligence must be established to prosecute medical professionals criminally.

subject: BNS
question: Abetment of suicide of child or person of unsound mind is punishable :-
explanation: Section 107 of BNS (Old IPC Section 305) deals specifically with abetment of suicide of a child or insane person.

subject: BNS
question: Abetment of suicide has been defined under which Section of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Section 108 of BNS (Old IPC Section 306) defines and penalizes general abetment of suicide.

subject: BNS
question: Which one of the following Sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 relates to punishment for 'Abetment to commit suicide'?
explanation: Section 108 BNS prescribes punishment of imprisonment up to 10 years and fine for abetment of suicide.

subject: BNS
question: To convict a person for offence under section 108 Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
options: Ingredients of section 45 Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 are to be proved.
Ingredients of section 45 Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 are not to be proved.
explanation: To establish an offence under Section 108 BNS, the baseline elements of abetment defined under Section 45 BNS (instigation, conspiracy, or intentional aid) must be established.

subject: BNS
question: A was found to have attempted suicide. A however was not successful. Investigation revealed that B had instigated A to attempt suicide. What are the consequences which will follow?
options: A shall be liable to be punished under Section 226 for attempt to suicide, and B shall be liable to be punished for Abetment for attempt to suicide.
Neither A nor B shall be liable for any punishment.
A shall not be punished, but B shall be punished for Abetment of attempt to suicide.
A shall be liable to be punished for offences under Section 226, and B is not liable to any punishment.
explanation: Attempt to suicide per se is decriminalized/restricted under Mental Healthcare Act framework and Section 226 BNS requirements, affecting corresponding abetment claims. (Option B maintained strictly as per source text key).

subject: BNS
question: Which Section of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 provides punishment for offence of attempt to murder :-
explanation: Section 109 of BNS (Old IPC Section 307) penalizes attempt to murder.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' shoots at 'Z' with intention to kill him, under such circumstances that, if death ensued, 'A' would be guilty of murder. 'A' is liable to punishment under :-
explanation: Illustration (a) to Section 109 BNS; shooting with intent to kill constitutes attempt to murder under Section 109.

subject: BNS
question: Sohan with intention of causing death of a child of tender years exposes him in a desert place. Sohan is liable under which section of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 :-
explanation: Exposing a child with specific intention to cause death constitutes attempt to murder under Section 109 BNS (Illustration c).

subject: BNS
question: 'A' with the intention of causing the death of a child of tender age, exposes it in deserted place, but death of the child does not ensue. 'A' has committed an offence of:-
explanation: Illustration (c) to Section 109 BNS explicitly categorizes this act as an Attempt to Murder.

subject: BNS
question: A, with the intent of causing mischief on B, sas fire to his house. Unknown to A, X was sleeping in the house at the time. X narrowy escapes the fire, and suffers serious burn injuries, and is hospitalized for 3 weeks. A did not have an enmity against X, and displayed great remorse for the fact that X got hurt. Which of the following is true ?
options: A has voluntarily committed attempt to murder and grievous hurt of X.
A has involuntarily committed attempt to murder and grievous hurt of X.
A has not committed any offence as there was no mens rea and A was remorseful.
A has voluntarily committed attempt to murder, but has not committed grievous hurt.
explanation: Setting fire to an occupied house carries knowledge of imminent danger; under penal law knowledge imputes voluntariness for both attempt to murder and grievous hurt.

subject: BNS
question: 'A', intending to murder 'Z' by poison, purchases poison and mixes the same with food and delivers it to 'Z's servant to place it on Z's table. 'A' has committed :-
options: an offence of attempt to murder.
an offence of preparation to commit murder.
an offence of culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
explanation: Delivering poison to a servant to serve to the victim completes the stage of preparation and constitutes an attempt to murder under Section 109 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' denied food to his wife 'B' for several days by keeping her confined in a room with intention to accelerate her death, 'B' any how managed to escape. What offence 'A' has committed?
explanation: Starving a person in confinement with intention to cause death constitutes an execution act toward murder, amounting to Attempt to Murder under Section 109 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: A concerts and agrees with B for poisoning C in order to murder him, for which B agrees to procure the poison, but did not procure. A and B are guilty of :-
options: attempt to murder with the aid of Section 3(5)
explanation: Evaluated strictly according to the source key answer.

subject: BNS
question: Under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which of the following is not a punishable offence?
options: Making preparation of waging war against the Government of India
Making preparation to commit depredation on territories of power at peace with the Government of India
explanation: Mere preparation to commit murder is not penalised under BNS; liability starts at the stage of attempt (Section 109).

subject: BNS
question: Under which Section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, attempt to commit culpable homicide is punishable ?
explanation: Section 110 of BNS (Old IPC Section 308) penalizes attempt to commit culpable homicide.

subject: BNS
question: 'A', with intention to cause culpable homicide not amounting to murder hits 'B' with an iron rod on his head. Offence under Section 110 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is made out :-
explanation: For an offence of attempt under Section 110 BNS, the act and intention/knowledge are essential; causing actual bodily hurt merely attracts an enhanced penalty clause, making the nature of injury irrelevant to establish the basic offence.

subject: BNS
question: Which Section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 provides for Organised crime and its punishment ?
explanation: Section 111 is a newly introduced statutory provision in BNS defining organised crime and prescribing stringent penal sanctions.

subject: BNS
question: A group of how many persons may be called organised crime syndicate ?
explanation: Section 111(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS) defines an organised crime syndicate as a group of two or more persons acting in concert to commit organised crime.

subject: BNS
question: Whoever commits organised crime shall, if such offence has resulted in the death of any person, be punished with :-
options: death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine which shall not be less than 5 lakh rupees
death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine which shall not be less than 10 lakh rupees
death or imprisonment for life or imprisonment which may extend to 10 years, and shall also be liable to fine which shall not be less than 10 lakh rupees
imprisonment for life or imprisonment which may extend to 10 years, and shall also be liable to fine which shall not be less than 5 lakh rupees
explanation: Section 111(2)(a) of BNS prescribes death or life imprisonment, along with a mandatory minimum fine of ₹10 lakh, if organised crime results in death.

subject: BNS
question: Punishment prescribed for petty organised crime in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is:-
options: imprisonment for not less than six months which may extend to three years and fine
imprisonment for not less than one year which may extend to five years and fine
imprisonment for not less than one year which may extend to seven years and fine
imprisonment for not less than two years which may extend to ten years and fine
explanation: Section 112(2) of BNS provides that petty organised crime (like snatching, pocket-picking, ticket scalping) is punishable with imprisonment between 1 year and 7 years, along with a fine.

subject: BNS
question: Which Section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 provides for Terrorist act and its punishment ?
explanation: Section 113 is a newly added provision in BNS that explicitly defines terrorist acts and prescribes corresponding punishments.

subject: BNS
question: Who shall decide whether to register the case under Section 113 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 or under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967?
options: Officer not below the rank of Superintendent of Police
Officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police
explanation: Section 113(7) of BNS specifies that an officer not below the rank of Superintendent of Police shall decide whether to register the case under BNS or UAPA, 1967.

subject: BNS
question: A prostitute, suffering from communicable disease, has sexual intercourse with a man representing that she was free from any disease commits :-
explanation: Causing disease to another person falls within the express definition of 'Hurt' under Section 114 of BNS (Old IPC Section 319).

subject: BNS
question: "Hurt" as defined in Section 114 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is causing of the following to any person :-
explanation: Section 114 of BNS defines hurt as causing bodily pain, disease, or infirmity to any person.

subject: BNS
question:
In which of the following cases the accused is liable for the punishment of offence of hurt:-
I. Dragging by hair in aggressive manner
II. Fisting on face in the course of attack
III. Forceful kick on the back
IV. A push to disbalance the other
explanation: All listed physical acts cause bodily pain or temporary physical discomfort/infirmity, satisfying the definition of Hurt under Section 114 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: A, attacks B to disfigure his face permanently. A could not do so, but causes B severe bodily pain for ten days. A commits the offence of :-
explanation: Severe bodily pain must last for at least 20 days to qualify as Grievous Hurt under Section 116 Eighthly. Since it lasted only 10 days, A is liable for simple hurt under Section 115 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: The offence of grievous hurt has been defined in:
explanation: Section 116 of BNS (Old IPC Section 320) defines Grievous Hurt.

subject: BNS
question: How many kinds of hurts are included under grievous hurt under Section 116 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Section 116 of BNS enumerates 8 distinct clauses/categories of hurt designated as 'grievous'.

subject: BNS
question: A was beaten by B. In this act, A's shoulder was dislocated (not fractured). B is liable for:-
explanation: Dislocation of any bone or joint falls under Section 116 Seventhly of BNS, constituting Grievous Hurt.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' has knocked down two teeth of 'B'. 'A' has committed the offence of :-
explanation: Fracture or dislocation of a tooth is specifically designated as Grievous Hurt under Section 116 Seventhly of BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Two persons, 'A' & 'B' fight with each other. 'A' was having a blade with which 'A' inflicts injury on the face of 'B' leaving a permanent scar on the face of 'B'. 'A' is guilty of offence of causing :-
options: Grievous hurt by sharp cutting object
Grievous hurt by rash or negligent act
Simple hurt by sharp cutting object
Simple hurt by rash or negligent act
explanation: Permanent disfiguration of the face is Grievous Hurt under Section 116 Sixthly BNS, and using a blade attracts Section 118(2) BNS (dangerous sharp object).

subject: BNS
question: ..............designated as 'grievous hurt' under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
options: Any hurt which causes the sufferer to be during the space of fifteen days in severe bodily pain
Permanent disfiguration of the head or face
explanation: Section 116 BNS lists hurt endangering life and face disfiguration; option (d) is marked per source answer key.

subject: BNS
question: Which kind of hurt is not grievous?
options: Any hurt which causes the sufferer to be during the space of 10 days in severe bodily pain.
Permanent privation of the sight of either eye.
Privation of any member or joint.
explanation: To be grievous hurt under Section 116 Eighthly BNS, severe bodily pain must persist for a period of at least 20 days (not 10 days).

subject: BNS
question: Any hurt is 'grievous' if it causes the sufferer to be in severe bodily pain or unable to follow his ordinary pursuits during the space of:-
explanation: Section 116 Eighthly of BNS requires a duration of twenty days.

subject: BNS
question: Which hurt is not a grievous one?
options: Permanent privation of the sight of either eye
Permanent impairing of the powers of any joint
Suffering, of ten days from severe bodily pain
explanation: 10 days of bodily pain does not meet the 20-day statutory threshold under Section 116 Eighthly BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Which one is not grievous injury under the provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:-
options: Ten days in severe bodily pain
Privation of any member or joint
explanation: 10 days of bodily pain falls short of the 20-day minimum requirement for grievous hurt.

subject: BNS
question: Which of the act amounts to grievous hurt :-
explanation: Emasculation is expressly listed as the First category of Grievous Hurt under Section 116 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Which of the following doesn't fall under grievous hurt?
options: Temporary privation of the sight of either eye
Hurt which causes severe bodily pain to the sufferer for atleast 20 days
explanation: Section 116 Secondly BNS requires permanent (not temporary) privation of the sight of either eye.

subject: BNS
question: Under Section 116 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 which of following kinds of hurt is not designated as "Grievous Hurt" :-
explanation: Section 116 Sixthly specifies permanent disfiguration of the head or face (not chest).

subject: BNS
question: Which kind of hurt is not a grievous hurt :-
options: Disfiguration of the head or face
Privation of army member or joint
explanation: Evaluated strictly according to the provided source answer key.

subject: BNS
question: 'B' assaults 'A' using a sharp edged weapon, resulting in an injury which is 6 cm long and 1/2 cm deep in the right forearm of 'A', 'B' is liable to be charged for an offence punishable under :-
explanation: Evaluated strictly according to the provided source key.

subject: BNS
question: A gives a fist blow and causes dislocation of tooth of Z. A committed an offence punishable under Section...... of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
explanation: Dislocating a tooth is Grievous Hurt (Section 116), and voluntarily causing grievous hurt without dangerous weapons is penalized under Section 117(2) BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Dislodging a tooth by a fist blow is an offence punishable under :-
explanation: Section 117(2) BNS provides the general punishment for voluntarily causing grievous hurt.

subject: BNS
question: A intending or knowing himself to be likely to permanently disfigure Z's face, gives Z a blow which does not disfigure Z's face permanently, but which causes Z to suffer severe bodily pain for the space of fifteen days. Which of the following is correct?
options: A has voluntarily caused grievous hurt
A has voluntarily caused hurt, as well as grievous hurt
A has involuntarily caused grievous hurt
explanation: Under Section 117(1) Explanation BNS, a person who intends or knows himself likely to cause one kind of grievous hurt, and actually causes hurt, voluntarily causes grievous hurt.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' causes 'B' a superficial skin-deep injury by a sword. What offence is committed?-
explanation: A sword is a sharp cutting instrument; causing even simple hurt with it constitutes voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapon under Section 118(1) BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapon is punishable under :-
options: Section 115(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Section 118(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Section 117(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Section 118(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
explanation: Section 118(2) of BNS (Old IPC Section 326) punishes voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means.

subject: BNS
question: X shoots an arrow targeting the left eye of Y, which hits the right eye of Y, due to which Y loses the vision of his right eye. X has committed an offence punishable under Section............. of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
explanation: An arrow is a dangerous weapon/missile, and causing permanent loss of eye vision is Grievous Hurt, satisfying Section 118(2) BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Two persons, A & B fight with each other. A was having a blade with which 'A' inflicts injury on the face of 'B' leaving a permanent scar on the face of B. A is guilty of offence of causing :-
options: Grievous hurt by sharp cutting object
Grievous hurt by rash or negligent act
Simple hurt by sharp cutting object
Simple hurt by rash or negligent act
explanation: Permanent facial scarring constitutes disfiguration under Section 116 Sixthly BNS, inflicted via a sharp object (blade).

subject: BNS
question: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt to extort property or a valuable security or to constrain to do anything, which is, illegal or which may facilitate the commission of an offence is dealt under :-
explanation: Section 119(2) of BNS (Old IPC Section 329) penalizes voluntarily causing grievous hurt to extort property or constrain illegal acts.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' a Zamindar tortures a raiyat in order to compel him to pay his rent, 'A' is guilty of an offence in Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 under :-
explanation: Statutory illustration to Section 120(1) BNS (Old IPC Section 330 Illustration a); torturing to compel payment of rent constitutes an offence under Section 120(1).

subject: BNS
question: 'A', a police officer tortures 'B' to induce 'B' to confess that he has committed a crime. 'A' is guilty under which of the following provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:-
explanation: Section 120(1) of BNS (Old IPC Section 330) penalizes hurt caused to extort a confession or information regarding a crime.

subject: BNS
question: A, a police officer, tortures Z in order to induce Z to confess that he committed a crime.
options: A has committed an offence under Section 117(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
A has committed an offence under Section 123 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
A has committed an offence under Section 120(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
A has committed an offence under Section 122(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
explanation: Direct application of Illustration (a) to Section 120(1) BNS.

subject: BNS
question: A, a zamindar, tortures a raiyat in order to compel him to pay his rent, A is :-
options: A is guilty of an offence under Section 119(2) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
A is guilty of an offence under Section 120(1) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
A is guilty of an offence under Section 120(2) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
A is guilty of an offence under Section 121(1) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
explanation: Illustration to Section 120(1) BNS.

subject: BNS
question: What punishment may be awarded for the offence of voluntarily causing hurt to deter a public servant from his duty under Section 121(1), Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
options: Imprisonment upto three years or fine or both
Imprisonment upto five years and fine or both
Imprisonment upto seven years and fine or both
Imprisonment upto ten years and fine or both
explanation: Section 121(1) of BNS prescribes imprisonment for a term which may extend to five years, or fine, or both.

subject: BNS
question: Voluntarily causing hurt on grave and sudden provocation to a person is punishable under?
explanation: Section 122(1) of BNS (Old IPC Section 334) punishes voluntarily causing hurt on grave and sudden provocation.

subject: BNS
question: Voluntarily causing grievous hurt by use of acid is punishable under which Section of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Section 124 of BNS (Old IPC Section 326A & 326B) penalizes acid attack offences.

subject: BNS
question: Which one of the following is not an essential element of the offence of acid attack mentioned under section 124(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 :-
explanation: Section 124(1) requires permanent or partial damage, deformity, burns, maiming, or disfigurement; mere fleeting bodily pain does not constitute an acid attack offence under this section.

subject: BNS
question: A throws acid on B and causes grievous hurts to him. Under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, A is liable for minimum punishment of ?
explanation: Section 124(1) of BNS mandates a minimum punishment of 10 years imprisonment, which may extend to life imprisonment.

subject: BNS
question: Voluntarily attempting to throw acid on any person is punishable under which section of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Section 124(2) of BNS (Old IPC Section 326B) penalizes attempting to throw or administer acid.

subject: BNS
question: Ms. 'X' throws acid on Mr. 'Y' which causes partial deformity of his hand. The deformity heals completely upon treatment. Which of these statements is correct?
options: Ms. 'X' has not committed any offence under Section 124 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 since the deformity healed completely.
Ms. 'X' has not committed any offence under Section 124 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 since the victim was not female.
Throwing acid is not an offence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
Ms. 'X' has committed the offence under Section 124 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 since merely reversibility of the deformity is irrelevant for purposes of these offences.
explanation: Explanation 1 to Section 124 BNS states that permanent or partial damage/deformity need not be irreversible for the offence to be complete.

subject: BNS
question: In which case Hon'ble Supreme Court has directed to pay minimum compensation of Rs. 3,00,000/- per acid attack victim :-
options: Sujoy Mitra Vs. State of West Bengal
Vennagot Anuradha Samir Vs. Vennagot Mohandas Samir
Indra Vijay Alok Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh
explanation: In Laxmi v. Union of India (2014), the Supreme Court issued key directions including a mandatory minimum compensation of ₹3 lakh for acid attack victims.

subject: BNS
question: 'A', a renowned surgeon is tried for medical negligence under Section 125 Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. Which of the following is correct?
options: Negligence is negligence, no distinction can be drawn between negligence under civil or criminal law
explanation: As established in Jacob Mathew v. State of Punjab, criminal negligence under Section 125 BNS requires gross negligence and mens rea/culpability beyond mere civil negligence.

subject: BNS
question: Wrongful restraint has been defined under :-
explanation: Section 126(1) of BNS (Old IPC Section 339) defines Wrongful Restraint.

subject: BNS
question: Whoever voluntarily obstructs any person so as to prevent that person from proceeding in any direction in which that person has a right to proceed is :-
explanation: Direct definition of Wrongful Restraint under Section 126(1) BNS.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' threatens to set a savage dog at 'Z' if 'Z' goes along a path which 'Z' has a right to go. It is :-
explanation: Statutory illustration to Section 126(1) BNS; blocking a person's path in one direction constitutes Wrongful Restraint.

subject: BNS
question: 'N', a landlord after repeatedly demanding and not getting the rent of his flat from the tenant 'H', one day locked the flat in order not to allow 'H' to enter it, till he pays the rent to him. Which of the following offences has 'N' committed under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Preventing a tenant from entering his flat obstructs him from proceeding in a direction where he has a legal right to proceed, constituting Wrongful Restraint under Section 126 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Punishment for wrongful restraint is :-
explanation: Section 126(2) BNS specifies simple imprisonment (for a term extending to one month, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both).

subject: BNS
question: Whoever commits the offence of wrongful restraint shall be punished with :-
options: imprisonment upto one month or fine upto 500/- or both
imprisonment upto one month or fine upto 1000/- or both
imprisonment upto one month or fine upto 5000/- or both
imprisonment upto two months or fine upto 5000/- or both
explanation: Section 126(2) of BNS prescribes simple imprisonment up to one month or fine up to ₹5,000, or both.

subject: BNS
question: Wrongful confinement has been defined under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 :-
explanation: Section 127(1) of BNS (Old IPC Section 340) defines Wrongful Confinement.

subject: BNS
question: If a police officer arrested and detained a person in the lockup despite producing the bail order from the Court, police officer is guilty of:-
explanation: Detaining a person beyond circumscribing limits despite a valid release/bail order constitutes Wrongful Confinement under Section 127 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' causes 'Z' to go within a walled space and locks 'Z' in. 'Z' is thus prevented from proceeding in any direction beyond the circumscribing line of wall. 'A' has committed an offence of :-
options: endangering life and personal safety of Z
explanation: Illustration (a) to Section 127(1) BNS; total restraint within circumscribing boundaries is Wrongful Confinement.

subject: BNS
question: A places men with firearms at the outlets of a building, and tells Z that they will fire at Z if Z attempts to leave the building. What offence has A committed?
explanation: Illustration (b) to Section 127(1) BNS establishes Wrongful Confinement, while the threat of injury constitutes Criminal Intimidation.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' places men with firearms at the outlets of a building and tells 'Z' that they will fire at 'Z' if 'Z' attempts to leave the building :-
explanation: Direct application of Illustration (b) to Section 127(1) BNS.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' was on his journey by car from Delhi to Agra. 'B' met him in the way and requested for a lift up to Mathura, an intermediate town, 'A' acceded to his request, but on reaching Mathura, did not drop 'B' there in spite of his repeated requests. 'B' was carried over to Agra against his wishes.
options: 'A' is not guilty of any offence
'A' is guilty of offence of abduction
'A' is guilty of offence of wrongful confinement
'A' is guilty of using criminal force
explanation: Restraining a person inside a moving vehicle beyond his intended destination circumscribes his liberty, amounting to Wrongful Confinement under Section 127 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: A police constable compels a person to remain in police station on false case of theft and allowing him to go after receiving money from him. He is liable for :-
explanation: Unlawfully detaining a person at a police station satisfies the elements of Wrongful Confinement under Section 127 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: "A" a police officer without warrant apprehends "Z" who has committed murder:
explanation: Arresting a cognizable offender (murderer) without a warrant is authorized by procedural law, making it a lawful exercise protected under Section 37 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: In which one of the following sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 punishment for wrongful confinement is provided ?
explanation: Section 127(2) of BNS prescribes punishment for general wrongful confinement.

subject: BNS
question: Whoever wrongfully confines any person shall be punished with :
options: imprisonment upto six months or fine upto 1000/- or both
imprisonment upto one year or fine upto 1000/- or both
imprisonment upto one year or fine upto 5000/- or both
imprisonment upto two years or fine upto 5000/- or both
explanation: Section 127(2) of BNS provides imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to ₹5,000, or both.

subject: BNS
question: Which one of the following provision of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 relates to "Criminal Force"?
explanation: Section 129 of BNS (Old IPC Section 350) defines Criminal Force.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' intentionally pulls up a woman's veil without her consent, intending or knowing it to be likely that he may thereby injure, frighten or annoy her. 'A' is guilty of :-
explanation: Illustration (a) to Section 129 BNS; intentionally using force without consent to cause annoyance constitutes Criminal Force.

subject: BNS
question: Which one of the following is not an illustration of criminal force?
options: A removes the veil of a lady B causing annoyance to her
A shakes his fist at B
A pours boiling water in the bucket from which B was bathing
explanation: Shaking a fist at a person is an act making preparation/gesture, which constitutes Assault (Section 130 BNS), not Criminal Force (which requires physical force/contact).

subject: BNS
question: 'A' incites a dog to spring upon Z, without Z's consent, intending to cause injury, fear or annoyance to Z, 'A' has, under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 committed :-
explanation: Illustration (h) to Section 129 BNS; inciting an animal to cause motion/contact constitutes Criminal Force.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' incites a dog to spring upon 'Z' without 'Z's consent with the intention to annoy 'Z', Here 'A' has committed the offence of :-
explanation: Direct application of Illustration (h) to Section 129 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: A spits over B. A would be liable for the offence of :-
explanation: Spitting on another person without consent to cause injury/annoyance is an illustration of Criminal Force under Section 129 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Assault can be caused by :-
explanation: Section 130 of BNS (Old IPC Section 351) specifies that assault is committed by making any gesture or preparation that causes apprehension of criminal force.

subject: BNS
question: Assault can not be caused by :-
explanation: Explanation to Section 130 BNS states that mere words do not amount to an assault unless accompanied by gestures or preparations.

subject: BNS
question: Which of the following is not an illustration of assault?
options: 'A' takes up a stick saying to 'B', "I will beat you"
'A' threatens B to see him later on
'A' medically examines a woman 'B' without her consent
'A' throws brickbats into the house of 'B'
explanation: Threatening to see someone later on consists of mere words without present gestures or immediate apprehension of force.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' shakes his fist at 'Z' intending or knowing it to be likely that he may thereby cause 'Z' to believe that 'A' is about to strike 'Z'. 'A' has :-
explanation: Illustration (a) to Section 130 BNS; shaking a fist causes reasonable apprehension of imminent force, amounting to Assault.

subject: BNS
question: A without B's consent and with intent to cause injury, fear or annoyance to B incites a dog to spring upon B. A has committed :-
options: Negligent conduct with respect to animal
explanation: Evaluated strictly according to the source answer key provided.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' begins to unloose the muzzle of a ferocious dog, intending or knowing it to be likely that he may thereby cause 'Z' to believe that he is about to cause the dog to attack 'Z'. 'A' has:-
options: committed the offence of assault under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
committed the offence of attempt to commit assault.
committed the offence of criminal intimidation under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
explanation: Illustration (c) to Section 130 BNS; unloosing the muzzle is a preparation causing apprehension of attack, constituting Assault.

subject: BNS
question: A person pointing a loaded gun at another person shall be deemed guilty of :-
explanation: Pointing a firearm creates reasonable apprehension of imminent violence, establishing the offence of Assault under Section 130 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Under which one of the following sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, an assault or criminal force used in attempting to commit theft of property is punishable?
explanation: Section 134 of BNS (Old IPC Section 356) punishes using assault or criminal force in an attempt to commit theft of property worn or carried by a person.

subject: BNS
question: How many kinds of kidnapping are there in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:-
explanation: Section 137 of BNS (Old IPC Section 359) divides kidnapping into two types: (1) Kidnapping from India, and (2) Kidnapping from lawful guardianship.

subject: BNS
question: The offence of Section 137(1)(b) Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is basically against :-
explanation: Kidnapping from lawful guardianship under Section 137(1)(b) BNS is primarily an offence against the rights of the lawful guardian over the minor.

subject: BNS
question: "Lawful Guardian" in the context of kidnapping under Section 137(1)(b) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 includes:-
options: Any person lawfully entrusted with the care or custody of the minor
explanation: Explanation to Section 137(1)(b) BNS states that 'lawful guardian' includes any person lawfully entrusted with the care or custody of the minor or unsound person.

subject: BNS
question: In kidnapping the consent of minor is :-
explanation: Since kidnapping is an offence against the guardian, the consent of the minor child is legally immaterial.

subject: BNS
question: The word 'takes' in section 137(1)(b) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 signifies :-
explanation: The expression 'takes' under Section 137(1)(b) BNS implies physical movement or leading away of the minor out of the custody of the lawful guardian.

subject: BNS
question: Which one of the following is not an essential ingredient of the offence of kidnapping under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
options: Without the consent of lawful guardian
Out of the keeping of the lawful guardian
explanation: Kidnapping is a strict liability offence; proof of criminal intention (mens rea) is not required to establish the offence.

subject: BNS
question: For an offence of kidnapping, the age of victim minor male child should be :-
explanation: Under Section 137(1)(b) of BNS, the age limit for minors (both male and female) is under 18 years.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' and 'B' both are of 16 years of age. 'A' entices 'B' for marriage and takes her to another city. What offence has been committed by 'A'?
options: A is himself minor. Hence A has committed no offence.
explanation: Enticing a minor girl under 18 years out of lawful guardianship constitutes Kidnapping under Section 137 BNS; minority of the accused does not alter the criminality of the act.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' is seventeen years old daughter of 'B', 'C' without consent of 'B' takes 'A' for a tour of South India. 'C' has committed the offence of:-
explanation: Taking a girl under 18 years of age without her guardian's consent constitutes Kidnapping under Section 137(1)(b) BNS.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' meets a girl aged fifteen years in a park. She tells him that she is sixteen years of age and she is ill-treated at her house by her father and that she would be happy to be taken away from there. Thereafter 'A' takes the girl to his house and allows her to remain there. In this case :-
options: 'A' has committed no offence as the girl has come with him with her own consent.
'A' has committed no offence as the girl misrepresented her age and 'A' believed her matured and capable of consenting.
'A' has committed the offence of kidnapping of minor from the lawful guardian.
'A' has committed the offence of kidnapping and wrongful confinement.
explanation: Consent of the minor girl and bona fide mistake as to age are not valid defences against a charge of kidnapping under Section 137 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: A takes a girl out of the custody of her lawful guardians. Which of the following statements is a complete defence if A is charged under Section 137(1)(b) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 for kidnapping on the ground that the girl was below the age of 18 years when taken away?
options: The girl was a student in a college and could understand what was right or wrong for her.
The girl was maltreated by the guardians and A promised her a better life.
The girl looked more than 18 years of age and the accused had satisfied himself that she was more than 18 years of age.
explanation: Kidnapping from lawful guardianship is an offence of strict liability; none of the options (a), (b), or (c) offer a valid defence.

subject: BNS
question: A falsely promises an orphan village girl aged about 15 years for imparting good education and job prospects in the city. The girl accompanies A but in the city she neither gets education nor a good job. Can A be prosecuted for the offence of kidnapping from lawful guardianship under Section 137(1)(b) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
options: No, because she came along voluntarily
No, because the girl being orphan was not under the custody of lawful guardian
Yes, because the girl was a minor and was misled by A
explanation: An essential element of Section 137(1)(b) BNS is taking the minor out of the keeping of a lawful guardian. An orphan without a lawful guardian cannot be kidnapped under this specific clause.

subject: BNS
question: The case of S. Varadarajan v. State relates to :-
options: Section 366-A of I.P.C. [Now, Section 96 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023]
Section 364-A of I.P.C. [Now, Section 140(2) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023]
Section 363 of I.P.C. [Now, Section 137(2) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023]
explanation: S. Varadarajan v. State (AIR 1965 SC 942) is a leading decision explaining the distinction between 'taking/enticing' and 'allowing a minor to accompany' under Section 363 IPC / Section 137(2) BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Which one of the following is a continuing offence :-
explanation: Abduction is a continuing offence because the act continues as long as the victim is moved from place to place by force or deceit.

subject: BNS
question: Whoever by force compels, or by any deceitful means induces any person to go from any place, commit the offence of :-
explanation: Direct definition of Abduction under Section 138 of BNS (Old IPC Section 362).

subject: BNS
question: For the offence of abduction of person, abducted must be :-
explanation: Abduction under Section 138 BNS applies to any person irrespective of age (minor or major).

subject: BNS
question: For abduction the abducted person should be :-
explanation: Section 138 BNS refers to 'any person', making age irrelevant for abduction.

subject: BNS
question: Abduction can be committed against :-
options: A male or female person below 18 years only
explanation: Abduction applies universally to persons of any age or gender.

subject: BNS
question: Under Section 138 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 the offence of abduction may be committed with :-
options: a girl under 18 years of age
a boy under 16 years of age
none of the above is correct
explanation: Options (a), (b), and (c) represent specific conditions of kidnapping; abduction applies to any person without age or mental capacity restrictions.

subject: BNS
question: The offence of kidnapping a child for the purpose of begging is punishable under :-
explanation: Section 139 of BNS (Old IPC Section 363A) penalizes kidnapping or maiming a child for purposes of begging.

subject: BNS
question: For the purpose of section 139 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, 'Child' means :-
options: A male under 16 years of age
A female under 18 years of age
any person below 18 years of age whether male or female
explanation: Section 139(4) BNS defines a 'child' as any person under eighteen years of age.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' forcibly carries or entices 'B' away from his home in order that 'B' may be murdered. 'A' has committed the offence in Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 :-
explanation: Section 140(1) of BNS (Old IPC Section 364) punishes kidnapping or abducting in order to murder.

subject: BNS
question: Under which section of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, kidnapping for ransom is provided?
explanation: Section 140(2) of BNS (Old IPC Section 364A) covers kidnapping for ransom.

subject: BNS
question: The minimum punishment for which of the following offences is life imprisonment?
explanation: Section 140(2) BNS prescribes death or imprisonment for life as mandatory penalties for kidnapping for ransom.

subject: BNS
question: Punishment provided for kidnapping for ransom in Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is :-
explanation: Section 140(2) of BNS provides that whoever commits kidnapping for ransom shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and fine.

subject: BNS
question: Under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 punishment for the offence of importing girls from any country outside India is imprisonment upto 10 years if the age of the girl is under :-
explanation: Section 141 of BNS (Old IPC Section 366B) specifies the age limit of girls imported from foreign countries as under twenty-one years.

subject: BNS
question: Punishment for Trafficking of person is in :
explanation: Section 143 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS) defines and penalizes the offence of trafficking of persons (replacing Old IPC Section 370).

subject: BNS
question: Punishment under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 for habitual dealing in slaves is :-
options: imprisonment for ten years and fine
imprisonment for life and fine or death
explanation: Section 145 of BNS (Old IPC Section 371) provides that whoever habitually imports, exports, removes, buys, sells, traffics or deals in slaves shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

subject: BNS
question: Under which Section of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 offence of unlawful compulsory labour is punishable :-
explanation: Section 146 of BNS (Old IPC Section 374) criminalizes unlawfully compelling any person to labour against his will.

subject: BNS
question: Waging or attempting to wage war, or abetting waging of war against the Government of India is punishable under.of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
explanation: Section 147 of BNS (Old IPC Section 121) penalizes waging or attempting to wage war, or abetting the waging of war, against the Government of India.

subject: BNS
question: Whoever, wages war against the Government of India or attempts to wage such war shall be punished with :-
options: Death or imprisonment of life with fine
explanation: Under Section 147 BNS, waging war against the Government of India carries capital punishment (death) or imprisonment for life, along with a fine.

subject: BNS
question: Whoever wages war against the Government of India, or attempts to wage such war, or abets the waging of such war, shall be punished with :-
options: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, or with fine, or with both
imprisonment for life and shall also be liable to fine
death, or imprisonment for life and shall also be liable to fine
imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years and shall also be liable to fine
explanation: Direct statutory text from Section 147 of BNS; the sentence can be death, or life imprisonment, and a mandatory fine.

subject: BNS
question: Under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which attempt is punishable offence?
options: Attempts to wage war against the government of India.
Attempts to wage war against the government of any foreign State at peace with the Government of India.
Attempt to commit robbery or dacoity with armed deadly weapon.
explanation: All three listed attempt scenarios are explicitly penalised under specific substantive sections of the BNS (Sections 147, 153, and 310/312 respectively).

subject: BNS
question: 'A' joins an insurrection against the Government of India. 'A' has committed the offence of :-
options: Abetment of desertion of soldier, sailor or airman
Waging of war against the Government of India
explanation: Joining an armed insurrection against the state constitutes the overt act of waging war against the Government of India under Section 147 BNS (Illustration to Old IPC Section 121).

subject: BNS
question: Under which of the following sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 a conspiracy to wage war against the Government of India is punishable ?
explanation: Section 148 of BNS (Old IPC Section 121A) penalizes conspiracy to commit offences punishable by Section 147 (waging war).

subject: BNS
question: 'X' the chairman of a political party during an election campaign alleged that the ruling party was responsible for inflation, increase in crimes, scams and corruption, and hence exalted his party members to overthrow the present government. Which of the following statements will be correct?
options: X is guilty as he was provoking his party men to overthrow the government
X is not guilty as his act does not amount to preparation for waging war against the government
X is not liable as what he was saying was true
X is liable as he was making an irresponsible statement
explanation: Political speeches and electoral rhetoric criticizing the government do not satisfy the legal threshold of waging war or preparation to wage war under Section 147/149 BNS without an intention or act to use armed force or violent insurrection against the state.

subject: BNS
question: Punishment prescribed in Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 for act endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India is :-
options: death or imprisonment for life with fine
explanation: Section 152 of BNS (the newly framed section replacing sedition) provides for punishment of imprisonment for life or imprisonment of either description which may extend to seven years, and fine.

subject: BNS
question: Waging war against Government of any foreign State at peace with Government of India is punishable under which Section of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 ?
explanation: Section 153 of BNS (Old IPC Section 125) punishes waging war against the government of any foreign State at peace with the Government of India.

subject: BNS
question: In which of the following Sections of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 'preparation' is punishable?
explanation: Preparation is punishable under Section 149 (collecting arms to wage war), Section 154 (committing depredation on friendly territories), and Section 310(4) (making preparation to commit dacoity).

subject: BNS
question: Which one of the following is not punishable under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
options: Preparation to wage war against the State
Preparation to commit depredation on the territory of a friendly power
explanation: Preparation to commit murder is not penalised under the BNS; criminal liability for murder begins at the stage of attempt (Section 109 BNS).

subject: BNS
question: Chapter 8 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is related with :-
options: Offences relating to the army, navy and air force
Offences by or relating to public servants
explanation: Chapter VIII of BNS deals with offences relating to the Army, Navy, and Air Force.

subject: BNS
question: Which Sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 provide for the offences relating to the Army, Navy and Air force ?
explanation: Sections 159 to 168 of BNS encompass offences relating to the Armed Forces.

subject: BNS
question: If a person abets the committing of mutiny by a soldier, he shall be punishable under :-
explanation: Section 159 of BNS (Old IPC Section 131) deals specifically with abetting mutiny committed by an officer, soldier, sailor, or airman.

subject: BNS
question: Abetting mutiny is punishable with :-
options: Death sentence or imprisonment for life and fine
Imprisonment for life or imprisonment upto ten years and fine
Imprisonment for life or imprisonment upto seven years and fine
Imprisonment upto ten years and fine
explanation: Section 159 BNS provides that whoever abets mutiny shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and fine.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' is a soldier in Indian Army, his friend 'B' offers him partnership in his firm, and abets the desertion from Indian Army. 'B':-
options: has committed offence of waging war
has committed abetment of desertion of soldier
explanation: Inducing or abetting an armed forces member to desert service is punishable under Section 163 of BNS (Old IPC Section 135).

subject: BNS
question: Abetment of desertion of soldier is punishable with :-
options: Imprisonment for seven years or fine or both
Imprisonment for five years or fine or both
Imprisonment for three years or fine or both
Imprisonment for two years or fine or both
explanation: Section 163 of BNS specifies imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or fine, or both.

subject: BNS
question: Provision relating to harbouring deserter has been prescribed under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in :-
explanation: Section 164 of BNS (Old IPC Section 136) governs the offence of harbouring a deserter.

subject: BNS
question: Harbouring a deserter is an offence punishable under Section 164 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. If harbour is given by a wife to her husband :-
options: she will be punished under Section 164
she may be punished at the discretion of Court
provision of Section 164 does not extend to spouse
punishment of wife will depend upon the facts and circumstances of the case
explanation: The Exception to Section 164 of BNS expressly exempts a spouse who harbours or conceals a deserter husband/wife.

subject: BNS
question: The words 'Candidate' and 'Electoral Rights' have been defined under which Section of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Section 169 of BNS (Old IPC Section 171A) defines 'candidate' and 'electoral right'.

subject: BNS
question: "Bribery" is defined in :
explanation: Section 170 of BNS (Old IPC Section 171B) defines Bribery in the context of electoral processes.

subject: BNS
question: A, a candidate at an election propagated that he was Chalanti Vishnu and representative of Lord Jagannath himself and that any one who does not vote for him would be sinner against the Lord and the Hindu religion :-
options: He is guilty of committing the offence of undue influence at elections, punishable under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
he is not guilty of an offence under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, but his candidature shall be cancelled
He is not guilty under any law for the time being in force
He is guilty of the offence of personation at election
explanation: Inducing voters to believe that they will be rendered an object of divine displeasure or spiritual censure interferes with the free exercise of electoral rights, amounting to Undue Influence under Section 171 BNS (Old IPC Section 171C).

subject: BNS
question: Which Section of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 defines 'personation at elections'?
explanation: Section 172 of BNS (Old IPC Section 171D) defines personation at elections.

subject: BNS
question: Chapter X of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 deals :-
options: with false evidence and offence against public justice
with of offences relating to coin, currency-notes, bank-notes, and government stamps
with offences relating to weight and measure
explanation: Chapter X of BNS consolidates provisions regarding coins, currency notes, bank notes, and government stamps into a single integrated chapter.

subject: BNS
question: "Coin" is defined in which section of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: In the BNS framework, definitions and substantive provisions regarding coin and currency counterfeiting are incorporated under Section 178.

subject: BNS
question: Offence of counterfeiting coin, Government stamps, currency-notes or bank-notes is punishable with :-
options: imprisonment for not less than 7 years but which may extend to 10 years, and fine
imprisonment for not less than 10 years but which may extend to 15 years, and fine
death or imprisonment for life, or imprisonment upto 10 years, and fine
imprisonment for life, or imprisonment upto 10 years, and fine
explanation: Section 178 of BNS provides punishment of imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and fine.

subject: BNS
question: "Possession of forged or counterfeit coin, Government stamp, currency-notes or bank-notes" is punishable under:
explanation: Section 180 of BNS deals with possession of forged or counterfeit coins, stamps, or currency notes knowing them to be counterfeit.

subject: BNS
question: "Possession of forged or counterfeit coin, Government stamp, currency-notes or bank-notes" is punishable with :-
options: imprisonment which may extend to 3 years or fine or both
imprisonment which may extend to 5 years or fine or both
imprisonment which may extend to 7 years or fine or both
imprisonment which may extend to 10 years or fine or both
explanation: Section 180 of BNS prescribes imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.

subject: BNS
question: 'Unlawful Assembly' has been defined in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 under :-
explanation: Section 189(1) of BNS (replacing Old IPC Section 141) defines Unlawful Assembly.

subject: BNS
question: For an assembly to be unlawful it must have a common object of the kind specified in:-
explanation: Section 189(1) of BNS enumerates the five specific common objects required to render an assembly unlawful.

subject: BNS
question: For an unlawful assembly, the minimum number of persons required is :-
explanation: Section 189(1) BNS requires an assembly of five or more persons sharing a specified common object.

subject: BNS
question: The term 'unlawful assembly' means :-
options: An assembly of five or more persons
An assembly of five or more persons armed with lethal weapons
An assembly of five or more persons with a common object of doing a crime
An assembly of minimum two persons having common intention to commit a crime
explanation: An assembly becomes unlawful when five or more individuals assemble with one of the statutory common objects specified under Section 189(1) BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Which of these is not essential element of unlawful assembly?
options: commission of offence in prosecution of common object
explanation: 'Common Intention' is a principle of joint liability under Section 3(5) BNS. Unlawful assembly under Section 189 requires a 'Common Object', making common intention non-essential.

subject: BNS
question: Joining unlawful assembly armed with deadly weapons has been dealt with under of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
explanation: Section 189(4) of BNS (Old IPC Section 144) penalizes joining or continuing in an unlawful assembly armed with deadly weapons.

subject: BNS
question: Which of the following case is related to "Unlawful assembly"?
options: Mohan Singh and anr. Vs. State of Punjab, AIR 1963 SC 174
Lennart Schussler and another Vs. Director of Enforcement and another, AIR 1970 SC 549
Mangilal Vs. Sirgan Chand Rathi, AIR 1965 SC 101
Lallu Yaeshwant Singh Vs. Rao Jagdish Singh, AIR 1968 SC 620
explanation: Mohan Singh v. State of Punjab (1963) is a leading decision on the statutory headcount requirements and common object of an unlawful assembly.

subject: BNS
question: Provision of common object is given in:
options: Section 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Section 38 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Section 149 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Section 190 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
explanation: Section 190 of BNS (Old IPC Section 149) creates constructive criminal liability for offences committed in prosecution of a common object.

subject: BNS
question: Section 190 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:-
explanation: Unlike common intention (Section 3(5)), Section 190 BNS creates a specific, substantive offence attaching vicarious liability to every member of the assembly.

subject: BNS
question: For application of section 190 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 :-
options: The offender must be a member of unlawful assembly
The offence must have been committed in prosecution of the common object
explanation: Both conditions are mandatory: membership in an unlawful assembly and commission of the crime in prosecution of its common object (or known to be likely).

subject: BNS
question:
The ingredients of Section 190 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 are :-
1. Knowledge of the probability of the commission of the offence
2. Common intention
3. Unlawful objects stated in Section 189(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
4. Active participation in commission of crime.

Select the correct answer using the codes given below :-
explanation: Section 190 requires membership in an assembly possessing an unlawful object under Section 189(1) and knowledge of the likelihood of commission; active overt participation in the specific criminal act is not required.

subject: BNS
question: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: To attract the offence under Section 190 Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, it must be shown that the accused persons had done the incriminating act to accomplish the unlawful common object of the unlawful assembly

To attract the offence under Section 190 Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, it must be shown that the accused persons shared the knowledge amongst themselves that the act is likely to be committed in prosecution of the unlawful act.

To attract the offence under Section 190 Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, some overt act on part of a member of the unlawful assembly is necessary to render him liable under Section 190 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
explanation: Under the second part of Section 190 BNS, liability attaches if the members knew that the offence was likely to be committed in prosecution of the common object.

subject: BNS
question: Which one of the following correctly brings out the main distinction between Common Intention and Common Object?
options: Common intention creates specific offence whereas common object does not
Common intention as well as common object create specific offences
Common object creates specific offence whereas common intention does not.
Both common objects as well as common intention do not create specific offence
explanation: Section 190 BNS (Common Object) creates a specific substantive offence, whereas Section 3(5) BNS (Common Intention) is merely a rule of joint liability.

subject: BNS
question: Which one of the following brings out the distinction between Section 3(5) and 190 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
options: Section 190 creates a specific offence whereas Section 3(5) does not
Section 3(5) creates a specific offence whereas Section 190 does not
Section 3(5) as well as Section 190 create specific offences
Section 3(5) as well as Section 190 do not create specific offences
explanation: Section 190 creates a distinct constructive offence, whereas Section 3(5) acts as a rule of joint constructive liability without creating a stand-alone offence.

subject: BNS
question: Which one of the following recognizes the principle of vicarious criminal liability under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Both Section 3(5) (Common Intention) and Section 190 (Common Object) embody principles of joint/vicarious constructive criminal liability.

subject: BNS
question: Which of the following is false of Section 3(5) and Section 190 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
options: Section 3(5) does not by itself create any specific offence whereas Section 190 does so
Some active participation in crime is required in Section 3(5) while it is not needed in Section 190
Section 3(5) speaks of common intention while Section 190 contemplates common object
Section 3(5) requires at least five persons who must share the common intention while Section 190 requires at least two persons to share the common intention
explanation: Statement (d) is false because Section 3(5) requires at least two persons, whereas Section 190 requires at least five persons (an unlawful assembly).

subject: BNS
question: The difference between section 3(5) and section 190 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is:-
options: that whereas is section 3(5) there must at least be five persons, section 190 requires only two persons
that section 190 is only a rule of evidence whereas section 3(5) creates a specific offence and provides for its punishment
that section 3(5) requires active participation in action whereas in section 190 mere passive membership of the unlawful assembly is sufficient
that section 3(5) need not be joined with the principle offence, whereas section 190 must be combined with the principle offence
explanation: Section 3(5) requires physical participation or overt assistance, whereas passive membership in an unlawful assembly suffices under Section 190.

subject: BNS
question: Which of the following is false in respect of Section 3(5) and Section 190 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
options: Section 3(5) does not by itself create any specific offence whereas Section 190 does so.
Some active participation in crime is required in Section 3(5) while it is not so in Section 190.
Section 3(5) speaks of common intention while Section 190 contemplates common object.
Section 3(5) requires at least five persons who must share the common intention while Section 190 requires at least two persons to share the common intention.
explanation: Statement (d) reverses the statutory headcount requirements (Section 3(5) needs 2+ persons; Section 190 needs 5+ persons).

subject: BNS
question: Distinction between Sections 34 and 149 of IPC [Now, Sections 3(5) and 190 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023] has been authoritatively expounded by the Supreme Court in :-
options: State of Maharashtra v. M.H. George
Guru Deo Singh v. State of Punjab
Ram Kumar v. State of Haryana
Nanak Chand v. State of Punjab
explanation: In Nanak Chand v. State of Punjab (AIR 1955 SC 274), the Supreme Court authoritatively analyzed the distinctions between Section 34 (Common Intention) and Section 149 (Common Object).

subject: BNS
question: Rioting means use of force or violence by an unlawful assembly, or by a member thereof, in prosecution of common object of such assembly, as per :-
explanation: Section 191(1) of BNS (Old IPC Section 146) defines the offence of Rioting.

subject: BNS
question: Use of violence by a member of an unlawful assembly of five or more persons in furtherance of common object, will constitute :-
explanation: The addition of force or violence to an unlawful assembly constitutes Rioting under Section 191 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: To constitute the offence of riot under Section 191 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, there shall be :-
options: Use of force or violence by an unlawful assembly
Creation of a distinct or unsual force by an unlawful assembly
Possession of a deadly weapon by an unlawful assembly
explanation: The essential distinguishing element of rioting under Section 191(1) BNS is the actual use of force or violence by an unlawful assembly.

subject: BNS
question: Which of the following statements is not true?
options: Rioting and affray have been defined in sections 191(1) and 194(1) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 respectively
Rioting must be committed in public place, affray may be committed in any place
Rioting is punishable with imprisonment extending to two years, affray is punishable with imprisonment extending to one month
Rioting is committed by 5 or more persons and affray is committed by 2 or more persons
explanation: Statement (b) is untrue because Affray must strictly be committed in a public place, whereas Rioting can occur in any place (public or private).

subject: BNS
question: Which of the following statement is not a correct one?
options: An assembly which was not unlawful when it assembled, may subsequently become an unlawful assembly
Kidnapping shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to seven years
It is not defamation to make an imputation on the character of another person provided that the imputation be made in good faith
A riot involves minimum of three persons
explanation: Statement (d) is incorrect because rioting requires an unlawful assembly, which mandates a minimum of five persons.

subject: BNS
question: In Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, punishment for rioting is provided under :-
explanation: Section 191(2) of BNS provides the general punishment for rioting.

subject: BNS
question: Punishment for rioting under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is :-
options: imprisonment upto two years or fine or both
imprisonment upto three years or fine or both
explanation: Section 191(2) BNS prescribes imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or fine, or both.

subject: BNS
question: Rioting while armed with deadly weapons is punishable under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 in:-
explanation: Section 191(3) of BNS (Old IPC Section 148) punishes rioting while armed with a deadly weapon (up to 3 years imprisonment or fine).

subject: BNS
question: Which one of the following sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 uses the word 'wantonly' is :-
explanation: Section 192 of BNS (Old IPC Section 153) uses the term 'wantonly' regarding giving provocation with intent to cause rioting.

subject: BNS
question: Which one of the following sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 deals with vicarious liability?
explanation: Section 193 of BNS (Old IPC Sections 154–156) attaches vicarious criminal liability to owners/occupiers of land on which an unlawful assembly or riot takes place.

subject: BNS
question: Which one of the following sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is an extension of the principle of 'respondent superior' to criminal law?
explanation: Section 193 of BNS incorporates the doctrine of respondeat superior (master's responsibility) regarding land agents/owners.

subject: BNS
question: ......is an offence against the Public Tranquillity.
explanation: Affray is classified under Chapter XI of BNS as an offence against public tranquillity.

subject: BNS
question: Under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 the offence of affray has been defined in :-
explanation: Section 194(1) of BNS (Old IPC Section 159) defines Affray.

subject: BNS
question: Which offence does not require minimum number of 5 persons ?
explanation: Affray requires a minimum of two persons, whereas Rioting and Dacoity both require a minimum of five persons.

subject: BNS
question: For affray under Section 194 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 the minimum number of person required is :-
explanation: Section 194(1) BNS states: 'When two or more persons, by fighting in a public place, disturb the public peace, they are said to commit an affray.'

subject: BNS
question: When two or more persons indulge in fighting at a public place and thereby commit breach of peace, they commit the offence of :-
explanation: Direct statutory definition of Affray under Section 194(1) BNS.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' and 'B' indulge in fighting and exchange blows in a cinema hall in the middle of a movie. They are guilty of :-
explanation: Fighting between two persons in a public place (cinema hall) disturbing public peace constitutes an Affray under Section 194 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: When two or more persons fight in a public place and commit breach of peace, they commit:-
explanation: Core statutory elements of Affray under Section 194 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: To constitute the crime of 'affray', what is necessary among the following?
explanation: Fighting in a public place is an indispensable ingredient of Affray.

subject: BNS
question: Which one of the following offences cannot be committed at a private place?
explanation: By definition, an Affray can only occur in a public place; fighting in a private place does not constitute an affray.

subject: BNS
question: Under the provision of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 fighting of two persons in a Public Place and disturbing the Public Peace will amount to :-
explanation: Direct statutory definition under Section 194(1) BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Which of the following statements is not true?
options: Rioting and affray have been defined in sections 191(1) and 194(1) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 respectively
Rioting must be committed in public place, affray may be committed in any place
Rioting is punishable with imprisonment extending to two years, affray is punishable with imprisonment extending to one month
Rioting is committed by 5 or more persons and affray is committed by 2 or more persons
explanation: Statement (b) is incorrect because affray requires a public place, whereas rioting can occur anywhere.

subject: BNS
question: What is maximum punishment that can be imposed on persons found to have committed the offence of affray ?
options: imprisonment which may extend to 1 month or fine which may extend to 1000/- or both
imprisonment which may extend to 2 months or fine which may extend to 1000/- or both
imprisonment which may extend to 3 months or fine which may extend to 2000/- or both
imprisonment which may extend to 6 months or fine which may extend to 5000/- or both
explanation: Section 194(2) BNS provides imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or fine up to ₹1,000, or both.

subject: BNS
question: Promoting enmity between different groups on grounds of religion is punishable under which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Section 196 of BNS (Old IPC Section 153A) punishes promoting enmity between different groups on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, etc.

subject: BNS
question: Under which one of the following sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 promoting enmity between different groups on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, etc. and doing acts prejudicial to maintenance of harmony has been dealt with?
explanation: Section 196 BNS contains provisions penalizing acts prejudicial to communal harmony.

subject: BNS
question: In an order in the Ashwini Kumar Upadhyay Vs. Union of India [Writ Petition (Civil) No. 943/2021] Case, the Supreme Court directed, inter alia, that States and Union Territories "shall ensure immediately, as and when any speech or any action takes place which attracts offences such as Section.........of Indian Penal Code etc., without any complaint being filed, suo motu action be taken to register cases and proceed against the offenders in accordance with law". The provisions of IPC stated by Supreme Court included:-
options: Sections 153A and 153B [Now, Sections 196 and 197 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023]
Section 295A [Now, Section 299 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023]
Section 506 [Now, Section 351(2)/(3) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023]
explanation: The Supreme Court directed mandatory suo motu registration of FIRs for hate speech offences covering all the specified sections.

subject: BNS
question: Imputations, assertions prejudicial to national integration have been provided under which of the following section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
explanation: Section 197 of BNS (Old IPC Section 153B) covers imputations and assertions prejudicial to national integration.

subject: BNS
question: Public servant disobeying a direction of the law with intent to cause injury is dealt under :-
explanation: Section 198 of BNS (Old IPC Section 166) penalizes a public servant knowingly disobeying a direction of law with intent to cause injury.

subject: BNS
question: A, being an officer directed by law to take property in execution, in order to satisfy a decree pronounced in Z's favour by a Court, knowingly disobeys that direction of law, with the knowledge that he is likely thereby to cause injury to Z. A has committed the offence defined in:-
explanation: Statutory illustration to Section 198 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: If a public servant fails to record an information of rape given under Section 173(1) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, he shall be punished under:
explanation: Section 199 of BNS (Old IPC Section 166A) punishes public servants who fail to record information regarding specified sexual offences.

subject: BNS
question: Under which section of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 the non-treatment of victim by public or private hospitals is punishable?
explanation: Section 200 of BNS (Old IPC Section 166B) penalizes the non-treatment of victims of acid attack/sexual offences by public or private hospitals.

subject: BNS
question: Contravention of the provisions of Section 397 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is:-
options: punishable under Section 166, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
punishable under Section 200, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
punishable under Section 207, Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
not punishable under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 but punishable under Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023
explanation: Section 397 BNSS mandates immediate medical treatment of victims; contravention is punishable under Section 200 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Whoever, being in charge of a hospital, public or private, whether run by the Central Government, the State Government, local bodies or any other person, contravenes the provisions of section 397 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 shall be punished u/s :-
explanation: Direct statutory cross-reference under Section 200 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: 'A' a private doctor running his own clinic, refuses to provide medical treatment to 'B', a victim of acid attack. He shall be punished under :-
explanation: Refusal to provide mandatory medical treatment to an acid attack victim is punishable under Section 200 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Whoever being in charge of a private or Public hospital contravenes the provisions of section 397 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 shall be punished with the imprisonment for a term which may extend to:
explanation: Section 200 BNS prescribes imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or fine, or both.

subject: BNS
question: Punishment for non-treatment of victim is :-
options: Imprisonment upto three months or fine or both
Imprisonment upto six months or fine or both
Imprisonment upto one year or fine or both
Imprisonment upto two years or fine or both
explanation: Section 200 BNS dictates imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both.

subject: BNS
question: X, the president of a hospital, refuses to treat A, who has been brought to his hospital while suffering from grievous hurt after a fight. X had some personal enmity against A, and did not wish to assist in saving his life. The ambulance therefore sped off to a nearby hospital where A was given treatment. Fortunately, A survived. Has X committed any offence?
options: X has not committed any offence
X has committed offences under Section 200 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
X has not committed any offence, but the offence under Section 200 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 would have been made out if A has not survived.
X is a doctor and is free to choose his patients. He can never be prosecuted for refusing to treat a patient, even if his actions are morally wrong.
explanation: Section 200 BNS specifically applies to non-treatment of victims of specified offences (like rape and acid attacks under Section 397 BNSS); general grievous hurt from an ordinary fight falls outside the penal scope of Section 200 BNS.

subject: BNS
question: Personating a public servant is an offence :-
options: Under Section 156 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Under Section 170 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Under Section 204 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Under Section 209 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
explanation: Section 204 of BNS (Old IPC Section 170) penalizes personating a public servant.

subject: BNS
question: 'A', being legally bound to appear before Raipur District Judge as a witness in obedience to a summons issued by court, intentionally omits to appear. 'A' is guilty under which of the following provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:-
